definition_zh: 蛙；青蛙；（马蹄后部的）蹄叉
definition_en: a small tailless amphibian with long hind legs for jumping that lives both in water and on land
core_image: 蹲在荷叶上鼓着眼睛、随时弹跳出去的小青蛙
scene: 雨后的池塘边一片湿润，草叶上还挂着水珠。 A green frog leaped off the lily pad and disappeared into the water with a splash.
sceneCN: 这里 frog 是「青蛙」（第 1 个义项：水陆两栖的小动物）；句意为一只绿蛙从睡莲叶上跳起，扑通一声消失在水里。

collocations.zh: 温水煮蛙（比喻慢慢恶化而不察觉）

derivatives.zh: 由名词 frog 加形容词后缀 -y 构成，义为「青蛙似的；（嗓音）沙哑的」
复合词 frog + man，义为「蛙人；水下作业潜水员」

senses.title: The small jumping amphibian
senses.definition: a small tailless amphibian that swims and leaps, starting life as a tadpole
senses.definitionCN: 一种无尾两栖小动物，会游泳会跳跃，幼体是蝌蚪
senses.example: The frog caught a fly with its long tongue.
senses.exampleCN: 青蛙用长舌头捕住了一只苍蝇。
senses.why: The word names the animal itself, so the sense grows straight out of the picture of a leaping pond creature.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名的就是动物本身，因此义项直接从「池塘里会弹跳的小生物」这一画面长出来。

senses.title: The spongy part of a horse's hoof
senses.definition: the soft V-shaped structure on the underside of a horse's hoof
senses.definitionCN: 马蹄底面柔软的 V 形结构，起减震作用
senses.example: The farrier cleaned the frog of the horse's hoof.
senses.exampleCN: 蹄铁匠清理了马蹄的蹄叉。
senses.why: The shape and springiness of this part reminded people of the animal, so the image of the frog was transferred to the hoof.
senses.whyCN: 这个部位的样子和弹性让人联想到青蛙，于是把「青蛙」的形象转移到了马蹄上，形成了这一专业义项。

senses.title: The frog-shaped fastener for clothing
senses.definition: an ornamental braided fastening, especially on Chinese-style coats
senses.definitionCN: 中式服装上用绳编织成的盘扣，形似青蛙
senses.example: The silk jacket closed with a row of frogs down the front.
senses.exampleCN: 这件丝质外套前襟用一排盘扣系合。
senses.why: Because the braided loops resemble a crouching frog, makers borrowed the animal's name for the fastener.
senses.whyCN: 因为编织的环扣形似蹲着的青蛙，制衣者借用了动物的名字来称呼这种扣件。

intro.en: Frog goes back to Old English, and its ultimate origin is uncertain, though many scholars connect it to words meaning to hop or croak.
intro.cn: frog 可追溯到古英语，其最终来源不确定，但许多学者把它与表示「跳、蛙鸣」的词联系起来。

items.en: Old English frogga and forsc named the pond amphibian.
items.cn: 古英语 frogga 与 forsc 用来指池塘里的两栖动物。

items.en: It belongs to a Germanic family of frog words, though no certain common root has been reconstructed.
items.cn: 它属于日耳曼语系里指蛙的一族词，但尚未重构出确定的共同词根。

items.en: Some scholars link it to an Indo-European base meaning to hop; others see it as imitative of the croaking sound.
items.cn: 一些学者把它与意为「跳跃」的印欧词基相联；另一些认为它是对蛙鸣声的拟声。

items.en: Middle English frogge carried both the animal sense and, later, the fastener sense.
items.cn: 中古英语 frogge 既指动物，后来也发展出扣件义。

items.en: Modern English keeps the animal as the core sense and adds hoof and clothing uses.
items.cn: 现代英语以动物义为核心，并发展出马蹄与服装的专业用法。

note.en: Frog is easy to confuse with several short animal and sound words.
note.cn: frog 容易和一些短小的动物词、拟声词混淆。

entries.definition: thick cloud of water droplets near the ground
entries.definitionCN: 雾；只是拼写与 frog 相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a dress, especially for a woman or girl
entries.definitionCN: 连衣裙；与 frog 拼写相近但毫无同源关系

entries.definition: a similar amphibian with a drier, warty body
entries.definitionCN: 蟾蜍；与青蛙同类但外形更干、有疣，词源独立

entries.definition: the larva of a frog or toad that lives in water
entries.definitionCN: 蝌蚪；蛙的幼体，与 frog 同属生活史链条

entries.definition: an amphibian of the same order, usually land-dwelling
entries.definitionCN: 蟾蜍；与 frog 同目不同科，常栖陆地

entries.definition: a small amphibian with a lizard-like tail
entries.definitionCN: 蝾螈；同为两栖动物但有尾巴，与 frog 相区分

normalIntro.en: Five real hooks for remembering frog.
normalIntro.cn: 五条基于真实词形与用法的 frog 记忆钩子。

normal.en: Frog shares its first letters with from, and the frog always leaps away from where it sat.
normal.cn: frog 的开头与 from 相同，青蛙总是从蹲着的地方弹跳离开。

normal.en: The phrase frog in one's throat literally puts a frog in your voice box.
normal.cn: 短语 frog in one's throat 字面是青蛙卡在喉咙，对应嗓子沙哑。

normal.en: A tadpole grows into a frog, so learn the two words as one life chain.
normal.cn: 蝌蚪长成青蛙，把 tadpole 与 frog 当作一条生命链来记。

normal.en: The adjective froggy uses the suffix -y to turn the animal into a quality.
normal.cn: 形容词 froggy 用后缀 -y 把动物名变成性质词。

normal.en: The fairy tale of the frog prince turns this word into a story hook.
normal.cn: 青蛙王子的童话把这个词变成了故事钩子。

abstract.en: Picture a frog crouching on a lily pad, eyes bulging, ready to spring.
abstract.cn: 想象一只青蛙蹲在睡莲叶上，鼓着眼睛蓄势待发。

abstract.en: Hear the two-beat croak, which almost repeats the word's own rhythm.
abstract.cn: 听那两拍蛙鸣，节奏几乎就是这个词本身的节奏。

abstract.en: Trace the arc of its leap, a curved line like a swelling letter.
abstract.cn: 描出它跳跃的弧线，像鼓起的字母曲线。

examples.en: A frog sat on the lily pad all afternoon.
examples.cn: 一只青蛙在睡莲叶上待了一下午。

examples.en: The children caught frogs by the pond and let them go.
examples.cn: 孩子们在池塘边捉了青蛙又放了。

examples.en: He cleared his throat, as if there were a frog in his throat.
examples.cn: 他清了清嗓子，像是有青蛙卡在喉咙里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「弗罗格」——青蛙先生姓弗罗格，蹲在池塘边呱呱叫。

root: 来源不确定：一般认为 frog 是古英语本土词，可能与表示「跳跃」的印欧词基有关，或为拟声词；无可靠的拉丁、希腊词根，不要强行拆解。

sensesIntro.en: The animal sense is the core; from it grow two figurative or specialized senses.
sensesIntro.cn: 动物义是核心；由它发展出马蹄与服装两个专业或比喻义项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small leaping amphibian by the pond
core.cn: 核心意象：池塘边会弹跳的小两栖动物

branches.en: the animal itself
branches.cn: 青蛙本体

branches.en: shape-based borrowings
branches.cn: 由形状引出的联想用法

branches.en: springy part of the hoof
branches.cn: 马蹄的弹性部位

branches.en: fastening loops on clothing
branches.cn: 服装上的盘扣

branches.en: springy, jumping qualities
branches.cn: 弹性与跳跃特质

intro.en: Frog is a short native word, so its word-building power comes from suffixes and compounds.
intro.cn: frog 是简短的本土词，构词能力主要体现在后缀与复合词上。

latinIntro.en: There are no Latin relatives because the word is Germanic and of uncertain origin.
latinIntro.cn: frog 属日耳曼语系且来源不确定，没有拉丁同源词。

items.meaning: like a frog; (of a voice) hoarse
items.example: He sounded froggy after the game.
A muddy, froggy pond attracted herons.
items.exampleCN: 泥泞多蛙的池塘引来苍鹭。

items.meaning: away, back (seen in from and fro)
items.meaningCN: 离去；向后（见于 from 与 to and fro）
items.example: She walked to and fro along the shore.
Boats shuttled to and fro on the river.

items.meaning: a frog that lives in trees
items.meaningCN: 树蛙；栖息在树上的蛙类
items.example: A tiny tree frog clung to a leaf.
items.exampleCN: 一只小树蛙紧贴在叶片上。

items.meaning: a diver equipped for underwater work

items.example: Each frogman wore a sealed suit.
items.exampleCN: 每名蛙人都穿着密封潜水服。

derivatives.zh: 青蛙似的；沙哑的

definition_zh: 混乱；脏乱；污物；困境；弄乱；食堂
definition_en: an untidy or dirty state; the waste left behind; a difficult situation; a group of people who eat together or the room where they eat; and as a verb, to make untidy or to spoil
core_image: 聚餐散场后，桌上盘盏堆叠，汤汁洒在桌布上，地上散落着碎屑
scene: 聚餐散场后，桌上的盘子还堆着，地毯上撒了饼干屑，厨房的门半开着。 After the dinner party, the kitchen was a complete mess.
sceneCN: 这里是「凌乱、脏乱」（第 1 个义项：东西没归位）；句意为聚餐结束后，厨房一片狼藉。图中可辨识物件：堆着的盘子、地毯上的碎屑、半开的门。

pos.zh: 混乱；脏乱；污物；困境；食堂

derivatives.zh: 由 mess 加 -y 构成，义为「凌乱的；脏乱的」
由 messy 去 y 加 -ly 构成，义为「凌乱地」
由 messy 去 y 加 -ness 构成，义为「凌乱；杂乱」

senses.title: An untidy, dirty state
senses.definition: a state in which things are not in order and look dirty or untidy
senses.definitionCN: 东西没有归位、看上去又脏又乱的状态
senses.example: After the dinner party, the kitchen was a complete mess.
senses.exampleCN: 聚餐结束后，厨房一片狼藉。
senses.why: The earliest mess was a portion of food served at table, so the modern sense of disorder still smells of the kitchen: plates, scraps and things left where they fell.
senses.whyCN: 最早的 mess 是端上桌的一份食物，所以今天「凌乱」这一义仍带着厨房气味：盘子、残渣，以及掉在哪里就留在哪里的东西。

senses.title: Dirt or waste left behind
senses.definition: dirty waste matter, especially the droppings of an animal, that somebody has to clean away
senses.definitionCN: 脏的废弃物，尤指动物的粪便，需要有人清理掉
senses.example: Watch the path, the dog leaves a mess on the grass every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 走路当心，那条狗每天早上都在草地上留下一摊脏东西。
senses.why: Once a mess is food that has been served and eaten, what remains on the ground is also a mess, so the word slides from the meal to its leftovers and then to any filth.
senses.whyCN: 既然 mess 是端上桌又被吃掉的食物，留在地上的残渣自然也是 mess，于是词义从饭菜滑向剩渣，再滑向一切脏东西。

senses.title: A difficult or confused situation
senses.definition: a situation full of trouble and confusion, especially one that someone has caused and must get out of
senses.definitionCN: 充满麻烦与混乱的局面，尤指自己造成、又必须脱身的局面
senses.example: He admitted his finances were in a mess after the failed deal.
senses.exampleCN: 他承认那笔交易失败后，自己的财务状况一团糟。
senses.why: When things are physically out of order, affairs can be out of order too, so the untidy room grows into a tangled situation with no easy way out.
senses.whyCN: 当东西在实处乱了套，事情也能乱套，于是凌乱的房间长成一团找不到出口的局面。

senses.title: To make untidy or to spoil
senses.definition: to make something dirty or untidy, or to spoil a plan or arrangement badly
senses.definitionCN: 把东西弄脏弄乱，或把计划、安排彻底毁掉
senses.example: He messed up the schedule by moving two meetings without telling anyone.
senses.exampleCN: 他没打招呼就挪动了两个会议，把日程搞乱了。
senses.why: The verb turns the noun into an act: to put something into a mess, or to ruin it the way a spilled plate ruins a laid table.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词变成动作：把东西弄成一团乱，或者像打翻一盘菜弄污摆好的桌面那样，把事情毁掉。

senses.title: A group that eats together, or its dining room
senses.definition: a group of people, especially soldiers, who eat together, or the room in which they eat
senses.definitionCN: 一起吃饭的一群人，尤指军人，或他们就餐的房间
senses.example: The officers gathered in the mess before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 军官们在黎明前聚到食堂。
senses.why: The first sense was a portion of food shared at one table; the people who shared it and the room where they shared it then took over the same name.
senses.whyCN: 最初的意思是同桌分享的一份食物；一起分享的人，以及他们分享所在的房间，后来都沿用了这个名字。

intro.en: Mess began as a word for a portion of food sent to table, and it reached English through French from a Latin verb meaning to send.
intro.cn: mess 起初指端上桌的一份食物，经法语进入英语，其源头是拉丁语中表示「送」的动词。

items.en: Mittere meant to send or to let go, and it supplied the verb behind a large family of sending words.
items.cn: mittere 意为送、放出，是这一大批与「送」有关的词共同的动词来源。

items.en: The noun missus named a course of food served at a meal, literally something sent to the table.
items.cn: 名词 missus 指用餐时端上的一道菜，字面意思是「被送到桌上的东西」。

items.en: Old French mes kept the food sense, meaning a portion or a dish, and also a group eating together.
items.cn: 古法语 mes 保留了食物义，指一份或一道菜，也可指一起进餐的一群人。

items.en: Middle English mess first meant a dish of food and a company of diners, especially in a household or an army.
items.cn: 中古英语的 mess 先指一盘食物和一群共餐者，尤用于家庭或军队。

items.en: Modern English pushed the word toward disorder in the eighteenth century, while the dining sense survived in military usage.
items.cn: 现代英语在十八世纪把词义推向「混乱」，而就餐义则在军队用语中保存下来。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words from the same Latin sending root; the near-meaning group collects words for disorder and jumble.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「送」词根上的词；近义组收表示混乱与杂乱的名词。

entries.definition: Untidy, dirty or complicated, said of rooms, hair or situations.
entries.definitionCN: 凌乱的、脏的或复杂的，可用于房间、头发或局面。

entries.definition: A piece of information sent to someone, from the same verb of sending.
entries.definitionCN: 送给某人的一条信息，同出「送」这一动词。

entries.definition: A person who carries a message from one place to another.
entries.definitionCN: 把消息从一处送到另一处的人。

entries.definition: An object thrown or fired, literally something sent.
entries.definitionCN: 被投出或射出的物体，字面即「被送出的东西」。

entries.definition: A lack of order, often on a larger scale than a messy room.
entries.definitionCN: 缺乏秩序，范围常比凌乱的房间更大。

entries.definition: A mass of small things lying about and taking up space.
entries.definitionCN: 散乱堆放着、占地方的一堆小东西。

entries.definition: Complete confusion in which nothing can be controlled.
entries.definitionCN: 彻底失控的混乱。

entries.definition: A confused mixture or a state of muddled thinking.
entries.definitionCN: 混杂的一团，或思路不清的状态。

normalIntro.en: The word rests on a Latin verb of sending; its family keeps returning to food sent to a table, the people around it, and the disorder left when the meal ends.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语表示「送」的动词上，同族词反复回到端上桌的食物、围桌的人，以及餐后留下的凌乱。

normal.en: Mittere in Latin means to send, and missus was a dish sent to the table.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 mittere 意为送，missus 就是被送到桌上的一道菜。

normal.en: Old French mes kept the food sense, so English mess first meant a portion or a dish, not a dirty room.
normal.cn: 古法语 mes 保留食物义，所以英语 mess 起初指一份或一道菜，而不是脏屋子。

normal.en: Because diners shared one dish, mess also named the group and the room where they ate, a sense still used in the army.
normal.cn: 因为同桌分食，mess 也指共餐的一群人与他们就餐的房间，这一义在军队中仍在用。

normal.en: Messy adds -y, meaning full of mess, and therefore untidy.
normal.cn: messy 加 -y，意为「充满 mess」，因此是凌乱的。

normal.en: Mess up is the verb phrase that turns the noun into the act of spoiling something.
normal.cn: mess up 这一动词短语把名词变成「把事情毁掉」的动作。

abstract.en: A word that once meant a shared dish now means disorder, which suggests mess is always what a good meal leaves behind.
abstract.cn: 一个曾经指共享菜食的词如今指混乱，这说明混乱往往是一顿好饭留下的残局。

abstract.en: The same word covers the food, the people eating it and the room they sit in, three parts of one ordinary evening.
abstract.cn: 同一个词覆盖了食物、吃饭的人与他们坐的房间，这是一个寻常夜晚的三个部分。

abstract.en: Calling a situation a mess borrows the picture of a table after dinner, because trouble is easier to bear when it looks like crumbs.
abstract.cn: 把局面称作 mess，是借用了餐后桌面的画面，因为麻烦一旦看起来像碎屑，就比较好承受。

examples.en: After the dinner party, the kitchen was a complete mess.
examples.cn: 聚餐结束后，厨房一片狼藉。

examples.en: He messed up the schedule by moving two meetings without telling anyone.
examples.cn: 他没打招呼就挪动了两个会议，把日程搞乱了。

examples.en: The officers gathered in the mess before dawn.
examples.cn: 军官们在黎明前聚到食堂。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「没洗」——碗没洗，厨房就乱成一团；记住 mess 是混乱。

root: 拉丁语 mittere（送）的分词名词 missus 指「端上桌的一道菜」，经古法语 mes（一份食物）进入英语；先指食物与共餐，后引申为凌乱与困境。

sensesIntro.en: The core is food sent to a shared table; the senses spread from the meal to its leftovers, then to disorder, to a troubled situation and to the room where a group eats.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是送到共享桌上的一份食物；义项从饭菜扩到残渣，再到凌乱、困境，以及一群人吃饭的房间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a table after a party, plates stacked high, gravy spilt on the cloth and crumbs scattered across the floor.
core.cn: 核心意象：聚餐散场后的桌面，盘盏高高堆起，汤汁洒在桌布上，碎屑散落一地。

branches.en: a sink piled with plates after a party
branches.cn: 聚餐后堆满盘子的水池

branches.en: crumbs and greasy marks across a table
branches.cn: 满桌碎屑与油痕

branches.en: a shoe scraping something off the grass
branches.cn: 鞋底在草地上蹭掉脏东西

branches.en: a desk buried under unsigned papers
branches.cn: 被未签文件埋住的办公桌

branches.en: a tray dropped at the door of a dining room
branches.cn: 食堂门口打翻的托盘

intro.en: The word is carried by a Latin verb of sending, its noun for a dish served, the French form, and English endings that build an adjective and a noun of state.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示「送」的拉丁动词、指上桌菜食的名词、法语形式，以及构成形容词与状态名词的英语词尾共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 最后；终于；完全地；最终地
definition_en: after a long time or after everything else, or in a way that ends something for good
core_image: 长队排到头的那一步：等了很久，终点终于踩到脚下
scene: 候车厅里的人已等了两个小时，广播忽然响起。 The delayed train finally pulled into the station.

senses.title: After a long wait
senses.definition: after waiting or trying for a long time, something happens
senses.definitionCN: 经过长久等待或努力之后，某事发生
senses.example: The rain finally stopped before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 雨终于在中午前停了。
senses.why: The core image is reaching the end of a long queue of time, so the sense adds relief.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是走完时间的长队，义项因此带上如释重负的语气。

senses.title: As the last item
senses.definition: used to introduce the last point in a list or speech
senses.definitionCN: 用来引出列举或讲话的最后一项
senses.example: Finally, remember to lock the door.
senses.exampleCN: 最后，记得锁门。
senses.why: The queue idea applies to spoken items as well as events.
senses.whyCN: 排队意象同样适用于话头：最后一项排在队尾。

senses.title: In a decisive, settled way
senses.definition: in a way that settles something completely and leaves no further dispute
senses.definitionCN: 以彻底解决、不再有争议的方式
senses.example: The border question was finally settled.
senses.exampleCN: 边界问题得到彻底解决。
senses.why: The final stroke ends not just a list but an argument.
senses.whyCN: 收尾的一笔结束的不只是清单，还有争论，于是长出定局义。

intro.en: Finally is simply final wearing an adverb ending.
intro.cn: finally 就是 final 加上副词词尾。

items.en: Latin finis meant an end or boundary.
items.cn: 拉丁语 finis 意为终点、界限。

items.en: Finalis described whatever stood at the end.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 finalis 形容处于末尾之物。

items.en: Old French final passed the adjective to English.
items.cn: 古法语 final 把形容词传给英语。

items.en: The adjective final was established in Middle English.
items.cn: 中古英语中形容词 final 已经定型。

items.en: The adverb finally formed with the native -ly ending.
items.cn: 现代英语用本族 -ly 词尾构成副词 finally。

note.en: Finally overlaps with at last and lastly, each with its own flavor.
note.cn: finally 与 at last、lastly 交叠，各自味道不同。

entries.definition: in small pieces or finely made; only one letter apart
entries.definitionCN: 细小地；精美地；与 finally 仅差一个字母

entries.definition: the adjective source of the adverb
entries.definitionCN: 形容词来源词

entries.definition: the quality of being final
entries.definitionCN: 定局性；同根名词

entries.definition: same relief, usually one clause long
entries.definitionCN: 终于，语气近似，多用于单句

entries.definition: introduces the last list item, no relief feeling
entries.definitionCN: 列举最后项，没有「久等」的意味

entries.definition: in the end, over a long period, less emotional
entries.definitionCN: 最终，强调长过程，情绪色彩更弱

normalIntro.en: Five hooks to hold finally in place.
normalIntro.cn: 五条钩子把 finally 安放妥当。

normal.en: Finally is final with -ly: the end word turned into a step.
normal.cn: finally 是 final 加 -ly：终点词变成了一个步骤。

normal.en: The bus finally came after an hour of waiting.
normal.cn: 等了一小时，公交车终于来了。

normal.en: Speech contest judges hear finally as the closing signal.
normal.cn: 演讲比赛的听众把 finally 当作收尾信号。

normal.en: Finally settled means the matter will not reopen.
normal.cn: finally settled 表示事情不会再翻案。

normal.en: Firstly, secondly, finally build a neat speaking ladder.
normal.cn: firstly、secondly、finally 搭出整齐的演讲梯子。

abstract.en: Finally is the last stair of a very long staircase.
abstract.cn: finally 是超长楼梯的最后一级。

abstract.en: Hear the door click: the wait is over.
abstract.cn: 听见门咔哒一声：等待结束了。

abstract.en: Everything before finally was just the road.
abstract.cn: finally 之前的一切只是道路。

examples.en: He finally passed the driving test.
examples.cn: 他终于通过了驾照考试。

examples.en: Finally, I want to thank my teachers.
examples.cn: 最后，我想感谢我的老师们。

examples.en: The dispute was finally settled last month.
examples.cn: 那场争端上个月得到最终解决。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「 faire 你」不对，用这个：「发你哦」——等了很久，结果终于发给你了；finally 就是终于发到你手上

root: 拉丁语 finis（终点）→ finalis → 古法语 final → 英语 final + 本族副词后缀 -ly；同根词有 finish、infinite。

sensesIntro.en: From relieved waiting to list endings and settled outcomes.
sensesIntro.cn: 义项从久等后的释然，走向列举收尾与彻底定局。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: stepping onto the last stair after a long climb
core.cn: 核心意象：长攀之后踏上的最后一级台阶

branches.en: the relief after waiting
branches.cn: 久等之后的释然

branches.en: the closing item of a speech
branches.cn: 讲话的收尾项

branches.en: the settled outcome
branches.cn: 彻底定下的结果

branches.en: the final stroke closes all
branches.cn: 收尾一笔终结一切

branches.en: the orderly speech ladder
branches.cn: 有序的演讲梯子

intro.en: Finally shows the native -ly adverb machine on a Latin adjective.
intro.cn: finally 展示了本族 -ly 副词机制套在拉丁形容词上。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root finis feeds the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 finis 支撑起整个词族。

Quick becomes quickly, final becomes finally.
items.exampleCN: quick 变 quickly，final 变 finally。
fin- 标记每个表示结束的词。
她的语气带着定局的意味。

items.example: The parade had a fireworks finale.
At last the exam was over.

definition_zh: 工程师；设计并建造机器、结构或系统的人；也指巧妙地安排或促成
definition_en: a person who designs and builds machines, structures or systems; also to arrange or bring something about by skill
core_image: 一个戴着安全帽的人蹲在图纸与实物之间，用手比量一处接缝，然后在纸上改掉一个数字
scene: 工地上，戴安全帽的人蹲在图纸与钢梁之间，用手比量一处接缝，又在纸上改掉一个数字。 The engineer changed one dimension and the whole frame became cheaper to build.
sceneCN: 这里 engineer 指设计并建造结构的人（第 1 个义项：工程师这一职业的人）；句意：这位工程师改动了一个尺寸，整个框架的建造成本便降低了。

derivatives.zh: 工程；工程学
经设计的
可工程化设计的（罕用）

senses.title: One who designs and builds
senses.definition: a person who applies technical knowledge to make machines, structures or systems work
senses.definitionCN: 运用技术知识使机器、结构或系统运转的人
senses.example: The engineer walked the site before agreeing to the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师先走了一遍现场，才同意那套方案。
senses.why: the -eer ending marks the agent, so the word begins as the person who works with engines.
senses.whyCN: 词尾标记施事者，因此这个词最初指与器械打交道的人。

senses.title: A licensed professional title
senses.definition: a formally qualified and often registered practitioner with legal responsibility for designs
senses.definitionCN: 具备正式资格、常需注册并对设计负法律责任的从业者
senses.example: Only a licensed engineer may sign the structural drawings.
senses.exampleCN: 只有持证工程师才能在结构图上签字。
senses.why: when public safety depends on a signature, the occupation becomes a protected title.
senses.whyCN: 当公共安全系于一个签名，这个职业就变成受保护的头衔。

senses.title: The one who runs an engine
senses.definition: the crew member responsible for a ship's or train's engines and machinery
senses.definitionCN: 船上或火车上负责发动机与机械的船员或乘务员
senses.example: The engine room answered to the engineer, not to the captain.
senses.exampleCN: 轮机舱听工程师的，而不是听船长的。
senses.why: the oldest everyday sense is the person in charge of the engine itself, a mechanic rather than a designer.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的日常义是掌管发动机本身的人，是技工而不是设计者。

senses.title: To design and construct
senses.definition: to plan and build something so that it meets a technical requirement
senses.definitionCN: 为使某物满足技术要求而规划并建造
senses.example: They engineered the tunnel to drain itself without pumps.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把隧道设计成无需水泵即可自排水。
senses.why: the noun's work becomes a verb the moment people speak of doing what the person does.
senses.whyCN: 当人们开始说「做这个人的事」，名词的工作就变成了动词。

senses.title: To arrange cleverly
senses.definition: to plan a situation so that a desired result follows
senses.definitionCN: 安排局面，使预期结果随之出现
senses.example: They engineered a delay that nobody could object to.
senses.exampleCN: 他们安排了一次谁也挑不出毛病的延迟。
senses.why: planned construction of a situation uses the same skill as planned construction of a bridge.
senses.whyCN: 安排局面与建造桥梁运用同一种「有计划的搭建」技能。

senses.title: To bring about by manipulation
senses.definition: to cause an outcome by quietly controlling the conditions
senses.definitionCN: 通过悄悄控制条件造成某个结果
senses.example: The result was engineered long before the vote.
senses.exampleCN: 那个结果早在投票之前就被促成了。
senses.why: the neutral verb darkens when the arrangement is hidden, because control without disclosure is manipulation.
senses.whyCN: 当安排被隐藏时，这个中性动词就变暗，因为不公开的控制就是操纵。

senses.title: A military builder of works
senses.definition: a soldier trained to build bridges, roads and fortifications
senses.definitionCN: 受训修筑桥梁、道路与工事的军人
senses.example: A military engineer surveyed the crossing before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 一名军事工程人员在黎明前勘察了渡口。
senses.why: the title was born in armies, where engines meant siege machines.
senses.whyCN: 这个头衔诞生于军队，那时「器械」指攻城机械。

senses.title: A software professional
senses.definition: a person who designs and maintains programs and systems
senses.definitionCN: 设计并维护程序与系统的人
senses.example: The engineer fixed the bug by removing a line, not adding one.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师删掉一行代码而不是加一行，就修好了那个缺陷。
senses.why: programs are now built things, so their builders inherit the old title without any metal involved.
senses.whyCN: 程序如今也是被建造之物，其建造者便继承了旧头衔，尽管不涉及金属。

senses.title: The on-site technical specialist
senses.definition: the person who installs, tests and repairs equipment where it is used
senses.definitionCN: 在使用现场安装、测试与维修设备的人
senses.example: A field engineer arrived with two replacement boards.
senses.exampleCN: 一位现场工程师带着两块备用板赶到。
senses.why: design and repair split into separate roles, and both keep the same broad title.
senses.whyCN: 设计与维修分成两种角色，两者都保留同一个宽泛头衔。

senses.title: One who alters living material
senses.definition: a specialist who redesigns genes or organisms
senses.definitionCN: 重新设计基因或生物体的专业人员
senses.example: The genetic engineer checked the sequence twice before proceeding.
senses.exampleCN: 基因工程师在继续之前把序列检查了两遍。
senses.why: the trade word follows its new materials, so a person who edits heredity is titled like a builder.
senses.whyCN: 行业词随新材料而延伸，编辑遗传的人也被冠以建造者式的头衔。

intro.en: Engineer is a person-word built on engine, from Latin ingenium, inborn talent. It began with military machines and widened to anyone who plans and builds.
intro.cn: engineer 是在 engine 之上构成的人物名词，而 engine 来自拉丁语 ingenium「天生才能」。它始于军用器械，后来扩大到一切规划与建造的人。

items.en: Latin ingenium meant natural talent and, by extension, a thing produced by talent, including a clever device.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ingenium 指天生的才能，引申指才能所造之物，包括巧妙的装置。

items.en: Old French engin meant both wit and a contrivance, and siege engines gave the word its military weight.
items.cn: 古法语 engin 兼指机智与装置，攻城器械给了这个词军事分量。

items.en: English engine covered any machine before steam narrowed it to a motor, a narrowing that came later than the person-word.
items.cn: 英语 engine 曾泛指任何机器，蒸汽时代才收窄为发动机，而这个收窄晚于人物名词的出现。

items.en: The engineer was first the soldier or craftsman who built and worked siege engines, then any builder of public works.
items.cn: engineer 最初指建造与操作攻城器械的士兵或工匠，后来指任何公共工程的建造者。

items.en: Roads, canals and railways turned military builders into civil professionals, and the title spread to every branch of construction.
items.cn: 道路、运河与铁路把军事建造者变成民用专业人员，这个头衔扩散到各个建造分支。

items.en: The twentieth century added software, genetic and financial uses, all sharing the sense of deliberate design.
items.cn: 二十世纪又添上软件、基因与金融用法，共同点是「有意的设计」。

note.en: The first group is the same root in its other roles; the second group is the neighbouring technical occupations.
note.cn: 第一组是同一词根的其他角色；第二组是相邻的技术职业。

entries.definition: The profession and activity; the engineer is the person inside it.
entries.definitionCN: 指职业与活动；engineer 是从事其中的人。

entries.definition: The motor or device itself; the person-word was formed from it, not the other way round.
entries.definitionCN: 指发动机或装置本身；人物名词由它构成，而不是反过来。

entries.definition: Deliberately designed, or brought about by arrangement, depending on the object.
entries.definitionCN: 指经有意设计，或指被安排促成，视宾语而定。

entries.definition: Belonging to the engineer, as in an engineer's drawing; it is not a separate word.
entries.definitionCN: 表示属于工程师，如「工程师的图纸」；它不是另一个词。

entries.definition: A person trained to run and maintain equipment; an engineer usually also designs it.
entries.definitionCN: 受训操作与维护设备的人；engineer 通常还要设计。

entries.definition: A person who repairs machines; the engineer may have designed what the mechanic fixes.
entries.definitionCN: 修理机器的人；engineer 可能正是设计了该机器的人。

entries.definition: A person who plans a form; the engineer's planning is constrained by physics and safety.
entries.definitionCN: 规划形态的人；engineer 的规划受物理与安全约束。

entries.definition: The designer of buildings; the engineer settles structure and services beneath that design.
entries.definitionCN: 建筑设计者；engineer 负责设计之下的结构与设备。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations from the real suffix and the real pair of noun and verb.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：来自真实词尾以及名词与动词的真实成对关系。

normal.en: The ending -eer marks a person, as in mountaineer and auctioneer.
normal.cn: 词尾 -eer 标记人物，如 mountaineer、auctioneer。

normal.en: The verb repeats the noun's forms: engineers, engineered, engineered, engineering.
normal.cn: 动词重复名词的形式：engineers、engineered、engineered、engineering。

normal.en: Two objects split the verb: engineer a bridge, engineer a delay.
normal.cn: 两类宾语分开动词：设计一座桥，促成一次延迟。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: civil engineer, chief engineer, field engineer.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：土木工程师、总工程师、现场工程师。

normal.en: The title began in armies and ended up in software, which shows how far a person-word can travel.
normal.cn: 这个头衔从军队开始，最后进了软件业，可见人物名词能走多远。

abstract.en: Picture a hand measuring a joint that exists only on paper, and the paper answering back.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在量只存在于纸上的接缝，而纸竟然回了话。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge that keeps a copy of its builder inside one of its bolts.
abstract.cn: 想象一座桥把建造者的影子留在一颗螺栓里。

abstract.en: Picture a schedule rearranged by someone who never touches the clock.
abstract.cn: 想象一张时间表被一个从不碰钟的人重新排列。

examples.en: The engineer refused to approve a joint she could not calculate.
examples.cn: 那位工程师拒绝批准一处她算不出来的接缝。

examples.en: They engineered the drainage so that the field would dry by itself.
examples.cn: 他们把排水设计得让田地能自行变干。

examples.en: A field engineer can fix in an hour what took a year to design.
examples.cn: 现场工程师能在一小时内修好设计花了一年才做出的东西。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「恩（en）机（gi）捏（neer）」——承恩于机器、亲手去捏的人，就是工程师

root: 拉丁 ingenium「天生才能」→ 古法语 engin「巧器」→ 英语 engine；加施事后缀构成 engineer，最初指造军用器械者，后泛指设计建造者，并转出动词用法。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses run from the designing professional through the licensed title, the engine operator, the two verb uses, military and software roles, field work and the editing of living material.
sensesIntro.cn: 十个义项从设计者出发，经过持证头衔、轮机操作者、两种动词用法、军事与软件角色、现场工作，最后到生物材料的改造者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a helmeted figure crouched between drawings and steel, measuring a joint and changing a number.
core.cn: 核心意象：戴安全帽的人蹲在图纸与钢梁之间，量一处接缝，改掉一个数字。

branches.en: BUILDERS OF THINGS: the general designer-builder, and the specialist who edits living material.
branches.cn: 建造者：泛指设计与建造的人，以及编辑生物材料的专家。

branches.en: TITLES AND ROLES: a licensed professional who signs drawings, a specialist on site, and the military builder of works.
branches.cn: 头衔与角色：在图纸上签字的持证者、现场作业的专员，以及军中修筑工事的人。

branches.en: ENGINE KEEPER: the mechanic in the engine room, the oldest everyday meaning.
branches.cn: 管机器的人：轮机舱里的技工，最古老的日常含义。

branches.en: BUILDING BY DESIGN: constructing to a requirement, and building programs rather than metal.
branches.cn: 按设计建造：按需求建造，以及建造程序而非金属。

branches.en: ARRANGING OUTCOMES: skilled arrangement in the open, and quiet manipulation behind it.
branches.cn: 安排结果：公开的巧妙安排，以及其背后的隐秘操纵。

intro.en: Engineer is engine with an agent ending; the same base then takes -ing for the field and -ed for the participle.
intro.cn: engineer 是 engine 加施事词尾；同一词基再加 -ing 成为领域名词，加 -ed 成为分词。

latinIntro.en: Latin ingenium is the deep base; French engin and the French agent ending -ier shaped the person-word before English took it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ingenium 是深远词基；法语 engin 与法语施事词尾 -ier 在英语借入前已塑成这个人物名词。

items.example: The noun already joins a person's gift to a made thing.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词已把人的天赋与造物连在一起。

items.example: French gave the base its military colour.
items.exampleCN: 法语给这个词基添上军事色彩。

items.example: The base names the thing the person works with.
items.exampleCN: 词基指这个人打交道的对象。

items.example: The ending is the same one seen in mountaineer.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾与 mountaineer 中所见相同。

items.example: The ending turns the person into a profession.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把人变成一门职业。

items.example: An engineered part has been through deliberate design.
items.exampleCN: 经工程设计的零件走过了有意的设计。

items.example: The ending marks what can be designed technically.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾标记可以被技术设计的东西。

items.example: Reverse engineering takes a product apart to learn it.
items.exampleCN: 逆向工程把产品拆开来学习。

definition_zh: 当地的；本地的；局部的；本地人；住处附近的酒吧；每站都停的慢车
definition_en: relating to a particular area or neighbourhood, affecting only one part of the body, a person who lives nearby, the pub nearest one's home, or a train that stops at every station
core_image: 街角一家小店的木牌上写着本街的名字，推门进去的人多半互相认识
scene: 周末的集市上，摊主把自家菜园刚摘的蔬菜摆上木桌，牌子上写着村子的名字。 We bought honey from a local farmer at the market.
sceneCN: 这里 local 是「当地的」（第 1 个义项：属于某一地方的）；句意为我们在集市上从一位当地农夫那里买了蜂蜜。图中可辨识物件：木桌、菜蔬、写着村名的木牌。

pos.zh: 本地人；住处附近的酒吧；慢车

derivatives.zh: 由 local 加 -ly 构成，义为「在当地；局部地」
由 local 加 -ity 构成，义为「地点；地区」
由 local 加 -ize 构成，义为「使限于局部；定位」

senses.title: Belonging to a particular area
senses.definition: belonging to or connected with a particular small area, town or neighbourhood
senses.definitionCN: 属于或与某一小片区域、城镇或街区有关的
senses.example: We bought honey from a local farmer at the market.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在集市上从一位当地农夫那里买了蜂蜜。
senses.why: Latin locus means place, and the adjective built on it simply marks whatever belongs to one place rather than to the whole country.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 locus 意为「地方」，由它构成的形容词只是标记某物属于某一处，而不是属于整个国家。

senses.title: A person who lives in the area
senses.definition: a person who lives in a particular area, especially as opposed to a visitor
senses.definitionCN: 住在某一地区的人，尤指相对于外来访客而言
senses.example: The locals were friendly and pointed us towards the old bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 当地人都很友善，还给我们指了去老桥的路。
senses.why: If an adjective can label anything of a place, it can stand alone as a name for the people of that place, so the adjective turned into a countable noun.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个形容词能标记属于某地的一切，它就能单独出来指那个地方的人，于是形容词变成了可数名词。

senses.title: The pub nearest one's home
senses.definition: in British informal speech, the pub close to where one lives and goes regularly
senses.definitionCN: 英式非正式说法，指住家附近、常去的那家酒吧
senses.example: We spent the evening at our local, talking to the barman.
senses.exampleCN: 我们晚上待在住处附近那家酒吧，和酒保聊天。
senses.why: British drinkers shorten the phrase the local pub to the local, so the adjective absorbs its noun and becomes a familiar place with a definite article.
senses.whyCN: 英国喝酒的人把 the local pub 缩成 the local，形容词吞掉了它修饰的名词，成了一个带定冠词的熟悉去处。

senses.title: Affecting only one part of the body
senses.definition: affecting only a small area of the body rather than the whole of it
senses.definitionCN: 只影响身体的一小块区域，而不是全身
senses.example: The dentist gave her a local anaesthetic before drilling.
senses.exampleCN: 牙医在钻牙之前给她用了局部麻醉。
senses.why: Medicine needed a word for treatment confined to one spot, and the adjective for belonging to a place was ready to mark a boundary inside the body.
senses.whyCN: 医学需要一个词来表示只限于某一处的治疗，而那个表示「属于某地」的形容词正好能在身体内部划出边界。

senses.title: A train that stops at every station
senses.definition: a train or bus that stops at every station along its route, in American usage
senses.definitionCN: 美式用法中指沿途每站都停的火车或公共汽车
senses.example: He took the local instead of the express and watched the small towns go by.
senses.exampleCN: 他坐了慢车而不是快车，一路上看着小镇慢慢退后。
senses.why: Railway timetables contrasted the express with the train serving each locality, and the name of the small place became the name of the slow service.
senses.whyCN: 铁路时刻表把快车与逐站服务各处的车对立起来，于是「小地方」的名字成了慢车的名字。

intro.en: Local goes back to the Latin word for place; the adjective travelled through French and then grew noun uses for people, pubs and trains.
intro.cn: local 可一直追到拉丁语中表示「地方」的词；这个形容词经法语进入英语，后来又长出指人、指酒吧和指慢车的名词用法。

items.en: Locus was the ordinary Latin noun for a place or a position, and its verb locare meant to put something in a place.
items.cn: locus 是拉丁语中表示地方或位置的普通名词，它的动词 locare 意为把某物放到某处。

items.en: Medieval Latin formed localis for whatever belongs to a particular place, and the adjective carried that narrow sense forward.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语造出 localis，指属于某一特定地方的东西，这个形容词把这层狭窄的意思继续传下去。

items.en: Old French used local as an adjective of place, and English borrowed it in the late fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语用 local 作为表示地方的形容词，英语在十四世纪晚期把它借了过来。

items.en: English applied local to parishes, customs and news, and in the nineteenth century began using it as a noun for the people and services of a place.
items.cn: 英语把 local 用于教区、习俗与新闻，并在十九世纪开始把它当名词，指一地的人和设施。

items.en: Modern English keeps local for the neighbourhood, medicine for a limited area of the body, British speech for the nearby pub, and American timetables for the stopping train.
items.cn: 现代英语用 local 指邻里，医学用它指身体的局部，英式口语用它指附近的酒吧，美式时刻表用它指逐站停靠的慢车。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers relatives built on the Latin word for place; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives that also mark where something belongs.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「地方」一词上的同族词；近义组收同样标记归属范围的形容词。

entries.definition: A particular area or neighbourhood.
entries.definitionCN: 地区；地点；由 local 加 -ity 构成。

entries.definition: To find the place of something or to place it.
entries.definitionCN: 找出某物的位置，或把某物安放在某处；来自拉丁语 locare。

entries.definition: The Latin noun for a place, still used in English for a particular point or site.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语中表示「地方」的名词，英语仍用它指某一位置或场所。

entries.definition: In or near a particular area.
entries.definitionCN: 在当地；在附近；由 local 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: Relating to a large area or district rather than a single town.
entries.definitionCN: 与较大的地区或区域有关，而 local 通常指更小的范围。

entries.definition: Relating to a province or to places outside the capital.
entries.definitionCN: 与外省有关，或指首都以外的地方。

entries.definition: Belonging to a place by birth rather than by residence.
entries.definitionCN: 因出生而属于某地，而 local 只强调居住或所在。

entries.definition: Located a short distance away.
entries.definitionCN: 位于不远处的。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on the Latin noun for place, and its family keeps returning to position, neighbourhood and the services of one small area.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语表示「地方」的名词上，它的同族词反复回到位置、邻里，以及某一小片区域的设施。

normal.en: Latin locus means place, so local is literally the adjective of a place, not of a whole country.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 locus 意为地方，所以 local 字面就是「属于某地的」形容词，而不是属于整个国家的。

normal.en: Locality adds -ity to local and names the area itself, while locate returns to the Latin verb for placing.
normal.cn: locality 在 local 后加 -ity，直接指那片区域；locate 则回到拉丁语中表示「放置」的动词。

normal.en: Local time is the time of one meridian, which is why a flight announcement always names it.
normal.cn: local time 是某一条经线上的时间，所以航班广播总要说明是当地时间。

normal.en: British speakers call their regular pub the local, shortening the local pub to one familiar word.
normal.cn: 英国人说 the local 指自己常去的酒吧，把 the local pub 缩成一个熟悉的词。

normal.en: A local train stops at each locality, so the adjective for small places became a noun for slow service.
normal.cn: local train 在每一个小地方都停，于是「小地方」的形容词变成了慢车的名词。

abstract.en: One adjective for place can name the people, the pub and the train, because all three are defined by being near.
abstract.cn: 同一个表示地方的形容词能指人、指酒吧、指火车，因为这三者都由「近」来定义。

abstract.en: Local and regional both answer where, but local draws a much smaller circle around the speaker.
abstract.cn: local 与 regional 都在回答「在哪里」，但 local 在说话者周围画出的圈小得多。

abstract.en: Medicine borrows the word to draw a border inside the body, showing how a place word can be used for any limited area.
abstract.cn: 医学借这个词在身体内部划一条边界，说明一个表示地方的词可用于任何有限的范围。

examples.en: We bought honey from a local farmer at the market.
examples.cn: 我们在集市上从一位当地农夫那里买了蜂蜜。

examples.en: The locals were friendly and pointed us towards the old bridge.
examples.cn: 当地人都很友善，还给我们指了去老桥的路。

examples.en: The dentist gave her a local anaesthetic before drilling.
examples.cn: 牙医在钻牙之前给她用了局部麻醉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「楼口」——楼下门口那家小店，来往的都是本街的人；local 是当地的，也是本地人。

root: 拉丁语 locus（地方）→ 中世纪拉丁语 localis（属于某地的）→ 古法语 local → 英语 local；同族词多与位置、地点、局部有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is belonging to one place; the senses then divide into the people of that place, the pub nearby, a limited part of the body, and a train that serves every small stop.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「属于某一处」；义项由此分成那地方的人、附近的酒吧、身体的局部，以及每个小站都停的慢车。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a corner shop whose wooden sign carries the name of this street.
core.cn: 核心意象：街角小店，木牌上写着这条街的名字。

branches.en: a farmer stacking vegetables on a market table
branches.cn: 农夫把蔬菜摆上集市木桌

branches.en: neighbours greeting each other at the shop door
branches.cn: 邻居在店门口互相打招呼

branches.en: a barman pulling a pint for a regular
branches.cn: 酒保给熟客打一杯酒

branches.en: a dentist preparing a small injection
branches.cn: 牙医准备一支小剂量的针

branches.en: a train halting at a country platform
branches.cn: 火车在乡间小站停下

intro.en: A Latin noun for place, its derived adjective and verb, one French borrowing and three English suffixes carry local from a point on a map to people, pubs and slow trains.
intro.cn: 一个表示地方的拉丁名词、由它派生的形容词与动词、一次法语借入，再加三个英语后缀，把 local 从地图上的一点带到人、酒吧与慢车。

latinIntro.en: Locus, localis and locare are all recorded Latin words built on the same stem for place and placing.
latinIntro.cn: locus、localis 与 locare 都是有记录的拉丁词，建立在同一个表示「地方、放置」的词干上。

definition_zh: 吵闹的；嘈杂的；热闹的；有噪声的
definition_en: making or full of loud sound, lively with many people, or containing unwanted random variation in a signal
core_image: 楼板把脚步和音乐一阵阵送下来
scene: 楼上那户人家的地板从晚饭后就没安静过，脚步和音乐声一直传下来。 The upstairs neighbours were noisy again, and the whole floor stayed awake.
sceneCN: 这里 noisy 是「吵闹的」（第 1 个义项：发出扰人的大声响）；句意为楼上的邻居又闹了起来，整层楼都没睡着。图中可辨识物件：楼上亮着的窗、木地板、床头的台灯。

pos.zh: 吵闹的；嘈杂的；热闹的；有噪声的

derivatives.zh: noisy 把词尾 y 改为 i 再加 -ly，义为「吵闹地」
由古法语 noise 进入英语，义为「噪音；喧闹声」
noisy 加 -ness，义为「吵闹；嘈杂程度」
由 noise 与 maker 复合，义为「发声玩具；制造响声的人」

senses.title: Making or full of loud, disturbing sound
senses.definition: making a lot of loud sound, or filled with sound that disturbs people
senses.definitionCN: 发出很大的声响，或充满扰人的声音
senses.example: The street outside the hotel was noisy all night.
senses.exampleCN: 旅馆外面的街道整夜都很吵。
senses.why: The suffix -y turns the noun noise into a quality, so a place or person can be described as carrying that sound wherever it goes.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -y 把名词 noise 变成一种性质，于是一个地方或一个人就被描述成走到哪里都带着这种声音。

senses.title: Lively with many people and sounds
senses.definition: full of people, music and activity in a way that feels lively rather than merely annoying
senses.definitionCN: 人多、有音乐、有活动，气氛活跃，而不只是令人烦躁
senses.example: It was a noisy party, with music and laughter in every room.
senses.exampleCN: 那是个热闹的聚会，每个房间都有音乐和笑声。
senses.why: Loud sound is not always a complaint; when many people gather happily, the same quality becomes a sign of life and energy.
senses.whyCN: 响亮的声音并不总是抱怨的对象；当许多人聚在一起高兴时，同一种性质就成了生气与活力的标志。

senses.title: Containing unwanted random variation
senses.titleCN: 有噪声的；夹杂随机误差的
senses.definition: containing random error or interference that hides the true signal, used of data, images or measurements
senses.definitionCN: 含随机误差或干扰，掩盖了真实信号，用于数据、图像或测量
senses.example: The sensor produced noisy data whenever the motor started.
senses.exampleCN: 马达一启动，传感器就会产生有噪声的数据。
senses.why: In technical use the unwanted sound of everyday life becomes unwanted variation in a signal, and the same word follows the metaphor.
senses.whyCN: 在技术语境里，日常生活里不受欢迎的声音变成信号中不受欢迎的波动，同一个词顺着这个比喻继续使用。

intro.en: Noisy is the noun noise plus the adjective ending -y; the deeper origin of noise is uncertain, and a suggested Latin link remains unproved.
intro.cn: noisy 是名词 noise 加形容词词尾 -y；noise 更早的来源不确定，与拉丁语的关联只是一种未获证实的猜测。

items.en: The ultimate source of noise is uncertain; a connection with Latin nausea is often suggested but cannot be confirmed.
items.cn: noise 的最终来源不确定；与拉丁语 nausea 的联系常被提出，却无法确认。

items.en: Old French noise named a quarrel, an outcry or a general din.
items.cn: 古法语 noise 指争吵、喊叫或一片喧闹。

items.en: Middle English took the word as a loud outcry and later narrowed it to unwanted sound.
items.cn: 中古英语借入时指大声喊叫，后来缩小为不受欢迎的声音。

items.en: Noise received the ending -y to form noisy, the adjective of a place or person full of sound.
items.cn: noise 加上词尾 -y 构成 noisy，用来形容充满声音的地方或人。

items.en: Modern English keeps the everyday sense and adds the technical sense of data disturbed by random error.
items.cn: 现代英语保留日常义，并增加了「数据受随机误差干扰」的技术义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the noise family and one word that merely resembles it; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives for high or overwhelming sound.
note.cn: 形近组收 noise 词族，另收一个只是形似的词；近义组收表示音量大或压倒性声响的形容词。

entries.definition: Unwanted or unpleasant sound; the noun behind noisy.
entries.definitionCN: 不受欢迎或令人不快的声音；noisy 背后的名词。

entries.definition: In a noisy manner; the adverb built from noisy.
entries.definitionCN: 吵闹地；由 noisy 构成的副词。

entries.definition: The quality or degree of being noisy.
entries.definitionCN: 吵闹的性质或程度。

entries.definition: Harmful or foul-smelling; it only looks like noisy and comes from a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 有害的或难闻的；只是拼写与 noisy 相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Producing a lot of sound; the plain adjective without the sense of disturbance.
entries.definitionCN: 发出很大声音的；不带「扰人」意味的一般说法。

entries.definition: Noisy and rough in a disorderly way.
entries.definitionCN: 吵闹而粗野、缺乏秩序的。

entries.definition: So loud that it seems to block out every other sound.
entries.definitionCN: 响得仿佛盖住其他所有声音的。

entries.definition: Full of loud and continuous demands or shouts.
entries.definitionCN: 充满响亮而持续的要求或呼喊的。

normalIntro.en: The word is noise plus -y, and its family keeps stretching the same quality from a room to a party and then to a signal.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 noise 加 -y，词族不断把同一种性质从一个房间延伸到一场聚会，再延伸到一段信号。

normal.en: Noise plus -y gives noisy: full of noise.
normal.cn: noise 加 -y 得 noisy：充满噪声的。

normal.en: The final y changes to i before -er and -est: noisier, noisiest.
normal.cn: 词尾 y 在 -er 与 -est 前变成 i：noisier、noisiest。

normal.en: Noisy describes a noun, while noisily describes how a verb is done.
normal.cn: noisy 修饰名词，noisily 则说明动词是怎么做的。

normal.en: A noisy party is not an insult: the same word can signal fun instead of disturbance.
normal.cn: 说一个聚会 noisy 并不是贬义：同一个词也能表示热闹好玩。

normal.en: In science, noisy data means measurements spoilt by random variation, not by actual sound.
normal.cn: 在科学语境里，noisy data 指被随机波动破坏的测量，而不是真的有声音。

abstract.en: A quality of sound becomes a description of a place, then of a mood, then of a measurement.
abstract.cn: 声音的一种性质，先变成对地方的描述，再变成对气氛的描述，最后变成对测量的描述。

abstract.en: The word shows how easily a nuisance turns into a sign of life, depending on who is listening.
abstract.cn: 这个词说明，同一件扰人的事多么容易变成生命力的标志，全看听的人是谁。

abstract.en: Noisy is the sound of a building with all its windows lit.
abstract.cn: noisy 是一栋窗户全亮着的楼发出的声音。

examples.en: The street outside the hotel was noisy all night.
examples.cn: 旅馆外面的街道整夜都很吵。

examples.en: It was a noisy party, with music and laughter in every room.
examples.cn: 那是个热闹的聚会，每个房间都有音乐和笑声。

examples.en: The sensor produced noisy data whenever the motor started.
examples.cn: 马达一启动，传感器就会产生有噪声的数据。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「闹一记」——有人闹，就留下一记声响；记住 noisy 是吵闹的。

root: noise 的来源不确定，一般认为经古法语 noise（喧闹、争吵）进入英语；与拉丁语 nausea 的联系未获证实。noisy 由 noise 加 -y 构成。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is full of sound; the senses then move to lively gathering and finally to unwanted variation in technical data.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是充满声音；义项由此转到热闹的聚集，最后转到技术数据里不受欢迎的波动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: floorboards passing footsteps and music down through the ceiling.
core.cn: 核心意象：楼板把脚步和音乐一阵阵送下来。

branches.en: an upstairs window still lit late at night
branches.cn: 深夜还亮着的楼上窗户

branches.en: a room full of music and laughter
branches.cn: 满是音乐与笑声的房间

branches.en: a screen of jagged readings
branches.cn: 一屏锯齿般的读数

branches.en: the same sound felt as nuisance or as fun
branches.cn: 同一种声音，被当作扰民，也被当作热闹

branches.en: a lively crowd and a disturbed signal
branches.cn: 热闹的人群与被干扰的信号

intro.en: The word is noise plus -y, and its family keeps adding endings and compounds to the same root of unwanted sound.
intro.cn: 这个词是 noise 加 -y，词族不断在「不受欢迎的声音」这个词根上添加词尾与复合成分。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded; the old suggestion of a link with Latin nausea has never been confirmed.
latinIntro.cn: 没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录；关于它与拉丁语 nausea 有关联的旧说法从未得到确认。

发声物品；制造响声的人

definition_zh: 地面；土地；场地；理由；基础； grounding（v.）使停飞； grounded
definition_en: the solid surface of the earth, an area for a purpose, or a reason for a belief
core_image: 脚踩住的那一层：一切楼、树、理由都从这里向上长
scene: 风筝越飞越远，孩子把它收回来抱在怀里。 The kite finally landed on the wet ground.
sceneCN: 这里 ground 是「地面」（第 1 个义项：土地的表层）；句意为风筝最终落在湿漉漉的地面上。

pos.zh: 名词：地面；土地；场地；理由；基础
动词：使停飞；使 grounded（禁足）；把……建立在

collocations.zh: 开辟新天地；开创新局面

derivatives.zh: 加后缀，义为「无根据的」

senses.title: The surface of the earth
senses.definition: the top layer of the earth that people and things stand on
senses.definitionCN: 人站立的地球表层
senses.example: The box lay open on the ground.
senses.exampleCN: 箱子敞开着躺在地上。
senses.why: The core image is the layer your feet trust, the starting sense.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是脚所信赖的那一层，这是最初的义项。

senses.title: An area used for a purpose
senses.definition: an area of land used for a particular activity
senses.definitionCN: 用于特定活动的土地
senses.example: The school ground was full at break.
senses.exampleCN: 课间操场上全是人。
senses.why: Part of the earth's surface is fenced off for one job.
senses.whyCN: 地表的一部分被圈出来专供一事。

senses.title: A reason or basis
senses.definition: a reason for saying, doing, or believing something, often plural
senses.definitionCN: 说话做事相信的理由，常用复数
senses.example: There are good grounds for his complaint.
senses.exampleCN: 他的投诉有充分的根据。
senses.why: Reasons are what an argument stands on.
senses.whyCN: 理由是论证所站立的地基。

senses.title: To stop a plane or a child from going
senses.definition: to keep a plane from flying, or a child from going out as punishment
senses.definitionCN: 不让飞机起飞，或不让孩子外出作为惩罚
senses.example: The airline grounded its fleet during the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴期间航空公司停飞了全部机队。

senses.whyCN: 被钉在地上者离不开地面，故有停飞与禁足。

definition_en: a person with deep knowledge or skill in a field, or having such knowledge and skill

senses.title: A person who knows a field deeply
senses.titleCN: 专家：把某个领域摸透的人
senses.definition: a person with a high level of knowledge or skill in a particular subject
senses.definitionCN: 在某一学科或领域拥有高水平知识或技能的人
senses.example: She is a leading expert on marine mammals.
senses.exampleCN: 她是海洋哺乳动物方面的顶尖专家。
senses.why: Latin expertus means 'tried, tested'. An expert is not someone who has merely read about a field but someone whose knowledge has been tested by the work itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 expertus 意为“试过的、验过的”。专家不是只在书上读过某个领域的人，而是其知识被实际工作检验过的人。

senses.title: A specialist called in to advise
senses.titleCN: 顾问专家：被请来出主意的人
senses.definition: a specialist whose advice is sought on a practical problem
senses.definitionCN: 就实际问题被请来提供建议的专门人才
senses.example: The company hired an expert to review its security.
senses.exampleCN: 公司请了一位专家来审查安保。
senses.why: The tested knowledge becomes useful to others. A person who has already walked the ground is called in so that others do not have to repeat every trial.
senses.whyCN: 被检验过的知识对别人有了用处。已经走过这条路的人被请进来，别人就不必把每一次试验都重做一遍。

senses.title: Expert witness in court
senses.titleCN: 专家证人：在法庭上提供专业判断
senses.definition: a witness allowed to give an opinion based on special knowledge rather than on what was directly seen
senses.definitionCN: 获准依据专门知识、而非亲眼所见来提供意见的证人
senses.example: The expert testified that the crack came from a fall.
senses.exampleCN: 这位专家作证说，裂痕是摔倒造成的。
senses.why: The legal sense is recorded from 1825. The courtroom needs knowledge that no ordinary witness could supply, so the tested person is placed in the witness box.
senses.whyCN: 这一法律义记录于 1825 年。法庭需要普通证人无法提供的知识，于是把“被检验过的人”放进了证人席。

senses.title: Skilled through long practice
senses.definition: adjective: highly skilled or experienced in doing something
senses.definitionCN: 形容词：做某事极为熟练或经验丰富
senses.example: He is an expert driver.
senses.exampleCN: 他是一位熟练的司机。
senses.why: The same past participle becomes an adjective: hands that have done the task many times are expert hands, whether or not the person is called an expert.
senses.whyCN: 同一个过去分词又变成形容词：反复做过这件事的手就是 expert hands，不管这个人是否被称为专家。

senses.title: Based on special knowledge
senses.titleCN: 专家的：依据专门知识作出的
senses.definition: adjective: coming from or based on specialized knowledge
senses.definitionCN: 形容词：来自专门知识或以其为依据的
senses.example: He gave expert advice on restoring the roof.
senses.exampleCN: 他就修复屋顶给出了专家建议。
senses.why: Advice is expert when it carries the weight of trials the listener has not run. The adjective marks the source of the knowledge.
senses.whyCN: 建议之所以是 expert，是因为它承载着听者没有做过的那些试验。形容词标记的是知识的来源。

senses.title: Done with mastery: an expert performance
senses.titleCN: 精湛的：做得像行家一样
senses.definition: adjective: done with great skill and control, especially in art, sport, or surgery
senses.definitionCN: 形容词：以极高技能与控制力完成，尤指艺术、运动或手术
senses.example: She gave an expert performance despite the pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管压力很大，她的表演依然精湛。
senses.why: The noun's 'tested person' becomes a quality of the action itself. A performance is expert when it looks as if trained hands are guiding every move.
senses.whyCN: 名词“被检验过的人”变成了动作本身的品质。当每一个动作都像由训练有素的手在引导时，表演就是 expert。

senses.title: Expert system: knowledge in a machine
senses.titleCN: 专家系统：装进机器里的专业知识
senses.definition: adjective, technical: designating a computer program that reproduces the decisions of a human specialist
senses.definitionCN: 形容词技术用法：指能重现人类专家判断的计算机程序
senses.example: The clinic uses an expert system to flag drug interactions.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所使用专家系统来标记药物相互作用。
senses.why: The knowledge of the tested specialist is written into rules. The machine inherits the adjective, though it has never tried anything itself.
senses.whyCN: 被检验过的专家的知识被写成规则。机器继承了形容词，尽管它自己从未“试”过任何事。

senses.title: Expert in, on, at: the fixed patterns
senses.titleCN: 固定搭配：expert in / on / at
senses.definition: in fixed phrases, expert in or on a field, and expert at doing something
senses.definitionCN: 固定短语中，expert in/on 接领域，expert at 接做某事
senses.example: She is expert at avoiding direct questions.
senses.exampleCN: 她很擅长回避直接提问。
senses.why: The preposition shows where the tested skill sits: in a subject, on a topic, at a performance. The adjective keeps the same 'proved by practice' core.
senses.whyCN: 介词显示被检验的技能落在哪里：in 接学科，on 接话题，at 接具体表现。形容词仍保留“经实践验证”的内核。

intro.en: Expert comes from Latin expertus, the past participle of experiri 'to try, test'. The adjective arrived first, in the late 14th century, meaning 'taught by experience'; the person-noun followed in the early 15th century.
intro.cn: expert 来自拉丁语 expertus，即 experiri“尝试、检验”的过去分词。形容词先到，14 世纪晚期意为“由经验教会的”；指人的名词随后于 15 世纪早期出现。

items.en: Experiri meant 'to try, test'. Its past participle expertus meant 'tried, tested, experienced', and peritus meant 'experienced, skilled'.
items.cn: experiri 意为“尝试、检验”。其过去分词 expertus 意为“试过的、验过的、有经验的”，peritus 意为“有经验的、熟练的”。

items.en: The root is traced to PIE *per- 'to try, risk'. The idea of danger and trial is built into the word: knowledge comes from attempts that could fail.
items.cn: 词根可追溯到原始印欧语 *per-“试、冒险”。危险与试炼的观念就嵌在词里：知识来自可能失败的尝试。

items.en: The English adjective is first recorded as 'experienced, taught by experience, skilled'. It describes a person or a hand that has been tested.
items.cn: 英语形容词最早记录为“有经验的、由经验教会的、熟练的”。它描述一个被检验过的人或一双被检验过的手。

items.en: The noun appears as 'a person wise through experience'. The adjective's tested quality is now attached to a person who can be consulted.
items.cn: 名词出现，意为“靠经验而明智的人”。形容词的“被检验”品质，现在附着在一个可以被请教的人身上。

items.en: The legal phrase expert witness is recorded in 1825: a witness selected for professional knowledge rather than for direct observation.
items.cn: 法律短语 expert witness 记录于 1825 年：证人因专业知识而非亲眼观察被选中。

items.en: Expertise, the noun for the knowledge itself, is borrowed from French in 1868. English keeps expert for the person or the adjective and expertise for the body of knowledge.
items.cn: 指知识本身的名词 expertise 于 1868 年借自法语。英语用 expert 指人或作形容词，用 expertise 指那一整套知识。

note.en: The first group shares spelling or word parts with expert; the second group shares meaning. Form first, then sense.
note.cn: 第一组与 expert 共享拼写或构词成分；第二组共享词义。先看词形，再看词义。

entries.definition: the knowledge and skill of an expert. Expert is the person or the adjective; expertise is the body of knowledge itself.
entries.definitionCN: 专家的知识与技能。expert 指人或作形容词；expertise 指那一整套知识本身。

entries.definition: a test carried out to find out something. It shares experiri 'to try'; an expert is a person shaped by many such tests.
entries.definitionCN: 为查明某事而做的实验。它共享 experiri“尝试”；专家则是被许多次这样的尝试塑造出来的人。

entries.definition: to carry goods out of a country. It is ex- + portare 'to carry', not periri 'to try'.
entries.definitionCN: 把货物运出国外。它是 ex- + portare“运送”，不是 periri“尝试”。

entries.definition: a person who concentrates on one branch of a subject, often medicine. Specialist stresses the narrow field; expert stresses the tested level of knowledge.
entries.definitionCN: 专注于某一分支（常指医学）的人。specialist 强调领域窄；expert 强调知识经过检验、水平高。

entries.definition: a person or work recognized as a source of reliable knowledge. Authority adds public recognition; expert adds tested skill.
entries.definitionCN: 被公认为可靠知识来源的人或著作。authority 多了公众认可；expert 多了被检验的技能。

entries.definition: a person who works in a skilled occupation. Professional stresses paid status and standards; an expert may be unpaid.
entries.definitionCN: 从事专业技能职业的人。professional 强调受薪身份与行业标准；expert 不一定以此为业。

entries.definition: a person with expert judgment in art, food, or wine. Connoisseur is about cultivated taste; expert is broader and can be technical.
entries.definitionCN: 在艺术、食物或酒方面有专家判断力的人。connoisseur 强调培养出的品味；expert 范围更广，可以是技术性的。

normalIntro.en: Real parts, real phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 真实的构词成分、真实短语和真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Experiri 'to try, test' is the core: an expert is a person whose knowledge has been tested by the work.
normal.cn: experiri“尝试、检验”是核心：专家就是知识被工作检验过的人。

normal.en: Expertus is the past participle 'tried, proved'. The adjective came first in the late 14th century; the person-noun followed in the early 15th.
normal.cn: expertus 是过去分词“试过的、验过的”。形容词在 14 世纪晚期先出现，指人的名词在 15 世纪早期跟上。

normal.en: Expertise is the noun for the knowledge, borrowed from French in 1868. Expert is the person or adjective; expertise is the body of knowledge.
normal.cn: expertise 是指知识的名词，1868 年借自法语。expert 指人或作形容词；expertise 指那一整套知识。

normal.en: Expert witness became a legal term in 1825: a witness chosen for knowledge rather than for what he or she saw.
normal.cn: expert witness 于 1825 年成为法律术语：证人因知识而非亲眼所见被选中。

normal.en: Do not confuse expert with export: export is ex- + portare 'carry', so it means carry goods out, not tested knowledge.
normal.cn: 不要把 expert 和 export 混淆：export 是 ex- + portare“运送”，意为把货物运出去，不是被检验的知识。

abstract.en: Picture a pair of hands that have repeated one task thousands of times. The knowledge is in the calluses before it is in any certificate.
abstract.cn: 想象一双把同一件事重复了上千次的手。知识先长在茧里，然后才写进证书。

abstract.en: A person is not an expert because of a title, but because a test has left a mark. Expertus means proved, not merely trained.
abstract.cn: 一个人成为专家，不是因为头衔，而是因为检验留下了痕迹。expertus 意为“被验证过的”，不只是“被训练过的”。

abstract.en: The expert stands at the edge of ordinary knowledge and is called in when the usual route runs out.
abstract.cn: 专家站在日常知识的边缘；当常规路径走不通时，人们就把他请进来。

examples.en: She is a leading expert on marine mammals.
examples.cn: 她是海洋哺乳动物方面的顶尖专家。

examples.en: The court heard expert testimony on the bullet's path.
examples.cn: 法庭听取了关于子弹轨迹的专家证词。

examples.en: He gave expert advice on restoring the roof.
examples.cn: 他就修复屋顶给出了专家建议。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱克死破特」——把难题“破”到底、试到头的人 → expert 专家、熟练的

root: 源自拉丁语 expertus「试过的、验过的」，是 experiri「尝试、检验」的过去分词，词根 per- 含“试、冒险”之意。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of expert, all built on one idea: knowledge proved by trial. The proved person can be consulted, can testify, can guide a hand, or can be written into a machine.
sensesIntro.cn: expert 的八个义项都建立在一个观念上：知识经过试炼而被证明。被证明的人可以被请教、可以作证、可以引导一双手，也可以被写进机器里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: hands that have tried the same task until the knowledge is proved.
core.cn: 核心意象：一双手把同一件事试到知识被证明为止。

branches.en: a person trusted for deep knowledge
branches.cn: 因深厚知识而被信任的人

branches.en: the specialist brought into court
branches.cn: 被请进法庭的专家

branches.en: the adjective of trained skill
branches.cn: 形容练出来的本事

branches.en: work done like a master
branches.cn: 做得像行家一样

branches.en: machine systems and set phrases
branches.cn: 专家系统与固定搭配

intro.en: Expert is formed from ex- 'out' and the per- stem of experiri 'to try'. English builds expertise, expertly and expertness directly on the finished word.
intro.cn: expert 由 ex-“出”和 experiri“尝试”的 per- 词干构成。英语直接在成品词上构成 expertise、expertly、expertness。

latinIntro.en: Latin experiri 'to try, test' gives the participle expertus and the noun experientia; peritus 'experienced, tested' shares the same root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 experiri“尝试、检验”生出分词 expertus 和名词 experientia；peritus“有经验的、经过检验的”共享同一词根。

items.meaning: a person proved by experience; skilled
items.meaningCN: 经经验证明的人；熟练的（ex- 出 + peritus 经过检验的）
items.example: They consulted an expert on soil.
items.exampleCN: 他们请教了一位土壤专家。

items.structure: expert + -ise (French noun of quality or skill)
items.meaning: the knowledge or skill of an expert
items.meaningCN: 专业知识；专长（-ise 构成性质名词，1868 年借自法语）
items.exampleCN: 这份工作需要技术专长。

items.meaningCN: 熟练地；内行地（-ly 构成副词）

items.meaning: a trial carried out to learn something
items.meaningCN: 实验；试验（尝试 + 名词后缀）

items.meaning: knowledge or skill gained by doing
items.meaningCN: 经验；经历（由“尝试”得来的知识）

items.meaning: based on experience rather than theory

senses.title: Not long ago
senses.definition: at a point in the near past, not long before now
senses.definitionCN: 在不久前的某个时点
senses.example: She recently joined the research team.
senses.exampleCN: 她最近加入了研究团队。
senses.why: The adjective recent means fresh in time, and -ly turns it into the adverb of a near past moment.
senses.whyCN: 形容词 recent 意为时间上新鲜的，加上 -ly 就成为表「不久前某一时点」的副词。

senses.title: Lately
senses.definition: during the period just before the present, seen as a stretch of time
senses.definitionCN: 在当下之前的一段时期里
senses.example: The weather has been unusually warm recently.
senses.exampleCN: 近来天气异常暖和。
senses.why: The same adverb covers a single moment and a stretch, because a recent period is made of recent moments.
senses.whyCN: 同一个副词既覆盖单个时点，也覆盖一段时期，因为「近期」正是由一个个「最近」组成。

senses.title: Newly in a role
senses.definition: at a time only shortly before now, especially after a change of status
senses.definitionCN: 在不久前，尤指身份刚发生改变之后
senses.example: The recently elected mayor promised reform.
senses.exampleCN: 新近当选的市长承诺推行改革。
senses.why: A change that has just happened leaves a person newly in a state, and the adverb marks that freshness of status.
senses.whyCN: 刚刚发生的变化让人处于一种新状态，这个副词正是标记身份的新鲜。

intro.en: Recently is the Latin adjective of freshness plus the English suffix of manner; a fresh moment becomes a fresh stretch of time.
intro.cn: recently 是拉丁语表新鲜的形容词加英语表方式的后缀；新鲜的瞬间由此变为新鲜的一段时间。

items.en: Recens meant fresh or just made, said of things still new.
items.cn: recens 意为新鲜的、刚做成的，用于仍然新的事物。

items.en: Old French recent carried the adjective into English without changing its sense.
items.cn: 古法语 recent 把这个形容词原样带入英语。

items.en: The native suffix -ly turns the adjective into an adverb of time and manner.
items.cn: 本族后缀 -ly 把形容词变为表时间与方式的副词。

items.en: Modern English uses recently for a near past moment and for the period just passed.
items.cn: 现代英语用 recently 指不久的过去时点，也指刚过去的一段时期。

items.en: The adverb widened from one moment to a whole stretch of recent time.
items.cn: 这个副词从单个瞬间扩展到整段近期时间。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the adjective base and two words close in sound; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs of the near past.
note.cn: 形近组收形容词原形与两个音近词；近义组收表「不久前」的副词。

entries.definition: Happening not long ago.
entries.definitionCN: 最近的。

entries.definition: In a proper and acceptable way.
entries.definitionCN: 得体地。

entries.definition: To feel bitter about something.
entries.definitionCN: 怨恨。

entries.definition: In the time just before now.
entries.definitionCN: 近来。

entries.definition: Only just, very recently.
entries.definitionCN: 新近地。

entries.definition: Just now, in a fresh state.
entries.definitionCN: 刚刚；新鲜地。

entries.definition: During recent times.
entries.definitionCN: 近来。

normalIntro.en: The word is recent plus ly: what is fresh in time becomes an adverb of the near past.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 recent 加 ly：时间上新鲜的东西，变成表「不久前」的副词。

normal.en: Recent plus -ly: in a recent way, or in recent time.
normal.cn: recent 加 -ly：以最近的方式，或在最近的时间里。

normal.en: Until recently means up to a point not long ago.
normal.cn: until recently 意为直到不久前。

normal.en: Recently arrived describes a person or thing that has just come.
normal.cn: recently arrived 形容刚到的人或物。

normal.en: The comparison is more recently, never recentlier.
normal.cn: 比较级是 more recently，绝不是 recentlier。

normal.en: Keep the t before ly: recently, not recenly.
normal.cn: ly 前要保留 t：recently，而不是 recenly。

abstract.en: Recently is where memory and news overlap, still warm enough to matter.
abstract.cn: 「最近」是记忆与新闻重叠的地方，还热得足以重要。

abstract.en: A thing done recently can still be undone; that is its power.
abstract.cn: 最近做成的事仍可被撤回，这就是它的力量。

abstract.en: We call the near past recent because we have not finished living it.
abstract.cn: 我们称近过去为「最近」，因为我们还没把它过完。

examples.en: She recently joined the research team.
examples.cn: 她最近加入了研究团队。

examples.en: The weather has been unusually warm recently.
examples.cn: 近来天气异常暖和。

examples.en: The recently elected mayor promised reform.
examples.cn: 新近当选的市长承诺推行改革。

dict_mnemonic.text: recent（最近的）加 ly（地）：最近的时点、近来的一段日子，都是 recently。

root: 拉丁 recens（新鲜的）→ 英语 recent + 后缀 -ly → recently；同族有 recency、recentness。

sensesIntro.en: The core is temporal freshness; the senses move from one near moment to a recent stretch and to a newly changed status.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「时间上的新鲜」；义项从一个临近的时点，到一段近期，再到刚改变的身份。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a message on a screen stamped just now.
core.cn: 核心意象：屏幕上一条刚收到的消息，时间标着「刚刚」。

branches.en: a screen stamped just now
branches.cn: 屏幕上刚打上的时间

branches.en: a warm week in a cold month
branches.cn: 寒冷月份里暖和的一周

branches.en: a newly elected mayor
branches.cn: 新近当选的市长

branches.en: a moment and a stretch of time
branches.cn: 一个瞬间与一段时间

branches.en: lately and newly
branches.cn: 近来与新近

intro.en: A Latin adjective of freshness takes two English suffixes, one for state and one for manner, to become an adverb of time.
intro.cn: 表新鲜的拉丁形容词接上两个英语后缀，一个表状态，一个表方式，成为表时间的副词。

latinIntro.en: The base recens is Latin, and the comparative recentior explains the English degree forms.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 recens 是拉丁语，其比较级 recentior 解释了英语的比较形式。

definition_zh: 过程；程序；流程；工序；（法律）程序；（计算机）进程；加工处理
definition_en: a series of actions or changes that leads to a result, or to handle something through such a series
core_image: 一条流水线：原料从一端进入，经过一道道工序，从另一端出来成品
scene: 面包房里，面团要经过发酵、整形、烘烤。 Fermenting, shaping and baking take four hours, and that process turns dough into something a shop can sell.
sceneCN: 这里 process 是「流程、工序」（第 1 个义项：为达到结果而进行的一系列动作）；句意：发酵、整形、烘烤要花四小时，这个流程把面团变成店里能卖的成品。图中可辨识物件：面团、发酵箱、整形台、烤炉、出炉的面包；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 过程；程序；流程；工序；（计算机）进程

derivatives.zh: 处理；加工
处理器；加工者
加工过的
行列；游行（同源异义）

senses.title: A series of actions toward a result
senses.definition: a set of actions taken in order to achieve a result
senses.definitionCN: 为达到结果而按序采取的一组动作
senses.example: The hiring process takes three weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 招聘流程需要三周。
senses.why: Latin processus is 'a going forward', from procedere. A process is a path with stages: it treats time as a route to be walked.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 processus 是“向前推进”，来自 procedere。process 是一条有阶段的路：它把时间当作要走完的路线。

senses.title: A natural series of changes
senses.definition: a course of natural changes that cannot be stopped
senses.definitionCN: 无法阻止的自然变化历程
senses.example: The process of decay begins at once.
senses.exampleCN: 腐烂过程立刻开始。
senses.why: Nature supplies the purest version: growth, erosion, decay. The word describes what happens by itself, without a planner.
senses.whyCN: 自然提供最纯粹的版本：生长、侵蚀、腐烂。这个词描述自行发生、没有规划者的事。

senses.title: A manufacturing procedure
senses.definition: the set of steps by which a product is made
senses.definitionCN: 制造产品所经的一组步骤
senses.example: The new process cuts production time in half.
senses.exampleCN: 新工序把生产时间缩短一半。
senses.why: Industry systematizes the path: each step has an input, an operation, and an output. Process becomes an engineered noun, and process engineering is born.
senses.whyCN: 工业把路径系统化：每一步都有输入、操作与输出。process 成了被工程化的名词，于是有了 process engineering。

senses.title: The legal course of proceedings
senses.definition: the formal steps required by law before a decision is valid
senses.definitionCN: 决定生效前法律要求的正式步骤
senses.example: The court must follow due process.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭必须遵循正当程序。
senses.why: Due process turns the path into a guarantee: the steps are not optional, and skipping one invalidates the result. Procedure and process converge here.
senses.whyCN: 正当程序把路径变成保障：步骤不可省略，跳过一步就使结果无效。procedure 与 process 在此汇合。

senses.title: A running program (computing)
senses.definition: an instance of a program running on a computer
senses.definitionCN: 计算机中正在运行的程序实例
senses.example: The process uses most of the memory.
senses.exampleCN: 这个进程占用了大部分内存。
senses.why: An operating system schedules tasks as a series of steps. Each running instance is a process, a path being walked by the machine.
senses.whyCN: 操作系统把任务安排成一系列步骤。每个运行实例就是一个 process，一条机器正在走的路径。

senses.title: To handle by a procedure
senses.definition: to deal with information or a request according to a set method
senses.definitionCN: 按既定方法处理信息或请求
senses.example: The computer processes thousands of forms a day.
senses.exampleCN: 计算机每天处理数千份表格。
senses.why: The verb turns the noun into action: to put something through the process. What is processed has entered the line and will come out changed.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词变成动作：把某物送进流程。被 processed 的东西已进入流水线，出来时会变样。

senses.title: To treat food or material
senses.definition: to change a raw material by physical or chemical treatment
senses.definitionCN: 通过物理或化学处理改变原料
senses.example: The factory processes milk into cheese.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂把牛奶加工成奶酪。
senses.why: Food processing is the clearest case: the input is real, the output is real, and the stages are visible. The word carries a neutral tone, though 'processed food' can sound negative.
senses.whyCN: 食品加工是最清楚的例子：输入真实，输出真实，阶段可见。这个词语气中性，尽管 processed food 听起来可能负面。

senses.title: To move in a procession (archaic)
senses.definition: in older usage, to walk in an ordered group
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法：按队列行走
senses.example: The choir processed down the aisle.
senses.exampleCN: 唱诗班列队走过通道。
senses.why: This archaic verb keeps the literal Latin walk. The noun procession is its surviving relative, still used for ceremonial lines of people.
senses.whyCN: 这个古义动词保留拉丁语字面的“走”。名词 procession 是它存活的亲戚，仍指礼仪性的人列。

senses.title: A bony projection (anatomy)
senses.definition: a natural outgrowth or prominence on a bone or organ
senses.definitionCN: 骨或器官上的自然突出部分
senses.example: The mastoid process lies behind the ear.
senses.exampleCN: 乳突位于耳后。
senses.why: Anatomy names protrusions 'processes' because they 'go forward' from the body of the bone. The Latin motion word becomes a shape word.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学把突出部分称作 process，因为它们从骨体“向前伸出”。拉丁运动词变成了形状词。

intro.en: Process began as 'a going forward'. Latin processus comes from procedere, 'to advance', and English first used it for the course of events, then for industrial and legal sequences, and finally for running programs.
intro.cn: process 最初意为“向前推进”。拉丁语 processus 来自 procedere“前进”，英语先用它指事件进程，再指工业与法律序列，最后指运行中的程序。

items.en: First recorded as 'the fact of being carried on; a course of events'.
items.cn: 最早记录为“被推进的事实；事件的进程”。

items.en: From Latin processus 'a going forward, advance, progress', from procedere 'go forward'.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 processus“前进、推进、进展”，源出 procedere“向前走”。

items.en: procedere = pro- 'forward' + cedere 'go'. The same verb gives proceed and procedure.
items.cn: procedere = pro-“向前”+ cedere“走”。同一动词生成 proceed 与 procedure。

items.en: The modern sense 'a continuous series of actions or changes' becomes established.
items.cn: 现代义“连续的动作或变化序列”确立。

items.en: Industrial use gives process engineering and manufacturing process.
items.cn: 工业用法产生 process engineering 与 manufacturing process。

items.en: Computing adopts the word for a running program, the newest link in the same chain.
items.cn: 计算机在 1960 年代采用这个词指运行程序，是同一链条上最新的一环。

note.en: The first group shares the cedere/procedere root; the second is about nouns that also mean a series of steps.
note.cn: 第一组共享 cedere/procedere 词根，第二组看同样表示“一系列步骤”的名词。

entries.definition: to go forward; the verb behind process.
entries.definitionCN: 向前走；process 背后的动词。

entries.definition: a prescribed set of steps. It stresses the rule, not the evolution.
entries.definitionCN: 规定的步骤。它强调规则，而非演化。

entries.definition: an ordered line of people moving. It keeps the literal walking sense.
entries.definitionCN: 有序行进的人列。它保留字面的行走义。

entries.definition: an official way of doing something. It is a process with authority behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 做某事的官方方式。它是有权威支撑的 process。

entries.definition: a planned way of doing something. It stresses design, not sequence in time.
entries.definitionCN: 有计划的做事方式。它强调设计，而非时间序列。

entries.definition: the way something develops over time. It is broader and less technical than process.
entries.definitionCN: 某物随时间发展的方式。它比 process 更宽、更少技术性。

normalIntro.en: Real links: Latin procedere 'go forward', the proceed/procedure/process family, due process, and the computing sense.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁语 procedere“向前走”、proceed/procedure/process 词族、正当程序，以及计算机义。

normal.en: Processus means 'a going forward'. A process is a path with stages, walked until something comes out.
normal.cn: processus 意为“向前推进”。process 是一条有阶段的路，走到某物出来为止。

normal.en: The verb behind it is proceed: pro- 'forward' plus cedere 'go'. Process is the noun of that walk.
normal.cn: 它背后的动词是 proceed：pro-“向前”加 cedere“走”。process 是那场行走的名词。

normal.en: Procedure is a process with rules attached: the same steps, now mandatory.
normal.cn: procedure 是附上规则的 process：同样的步骤，现在成了必须。

normal.en: Due process means the steps cannot be skipped; skipping one invalidates the result.
normal.cn: 正当程序意味着步骤不可跳过；跳过一步，结果就无效。

normal.en: In computing, a process is a program mid-walk: the machine is following its steps right now.
normal.cn: 计算机中，process 是走到一半的程序：机器正在执行它的步骤。

abstract.en: A process converts time into shape: what was merely passing becomes a route with stages.
abstract.cn: 过程把时间变成形状：原本只是流逝的东西，成了有阶段的路线。

abstract.en: Calling something a process can hide responsibility: nobody did it, it just went through its steps.
abstract.cn: 把某事称作 process 可以隐藏责任：没人做的，它只是走完了步骤。

abstract.en: Nature and factory share the word because both produce an output by ordered change.
abstract.cn: 自然与工厂共享这个词，因为两者都通过有序变化产出结果。

examples.en: Learning a language is a gradual process.
examples.cn: 学语言是一个渐进的过程。

examples.en: The application process is now fully online.
examples.cn: 申请流程现已完全在线。

examples.en: The plant processes raw cocoa into chocolate.
examples.cn: 工厂把生可可加工成巧克力。

dict_mnemonic.text: “扑若塞斯”——扑过去，像塞子一样一环环推进 → process 过程、流程

root: 拉丁语 processus“前进、推进”，源出 procedere“向前走”= pro-“向前”+ cedere“走”；同族有 proceed、procedure、procession。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of process, one path in different costumes. The path can be natural (decay), industrial (a production line), legal (due process), digital (a running program), or even anatomical (a bony projection).
sensesIntro.cn: process 的九个义项，是同一条路的不同装扮。这条路可以是自然的（腐烂）、工业的（生产线）、法律的（正当程序）、数字的（运行程序），甚至解剖的（骨突起）。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a route with stages, from input to output.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条有阶段的路，从输入到输出。

branches.en: COURSE: ordered change, whether planned or natural.
branches.cn: 历程：有序变化，无论有计划还是自然发生。

branches.en: MAKING: raw material enters a line and comes out changed.
branches.cn: 制造：原料进入流水线，出来时已变样。

branches.en: LAW: due process makes the steps mandatory and the result valid.
branches.cn: 法律：正当程序使步骤成为必须，使结果有效。

branches.en: COMPUTING: the path becomes a running program, and the verb means to put data through it.
branches.cn: 计算机：路径变成运行中的程序，动词意为让数据走一遍。

branches.en: SHAPE: the archaic walk survives in procession, while anatomy names protrusions 'processes'.
branches.cn: 形状：古义的行走存于 procession，解剖学则把突起称作 process。

intro.en: Process is noun and verb. English adds -ing, -or, and -ed, and the same Latin verb gives proceed, procedure, and procession.
intro.cn: process 既是名词也是动词。英语加 -ing、-or、-ed，同一拉丁动词还生成 proceed、procedure、procession。

latinIntro.en: Latin processus 'advance' comes from procedere 'go forward', built on cedere 'go'. The family is about ordered motion, from law courts to factory floors.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 processus“推进”来自 procedere“向前走”，建立在 cedere“走”上。这个词族关乎有序运动，从法庭到工厂车间。
