definition_zh: 丈夫；节约使用；管家
definition_en: the man that someone is married to, or to use resources carefully
core_image: 住在同一屋檐下、当家持户的人
scene: 婚礼上交换戒指之后。 She introduced the tall man as her husband.
sceneCN: 这里 husband 是「丈夫」（第 1 个义项：结婚对象中的男性一方）；句意：她介绍那位高个子男人是她的丈夫。

derivatives.zh: 丈夫般的；善持家的；加形容词后缀
农艺；节约管理；加名词后缀
家庭主妇；同族复合词

senses.title: A married man
senses.definition: the man to whom someone is married
senses.definitionCN: 某人所嫁的男性配偶
senses.example: Her husband cooks dinner every Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 她丈夫每周五做晚饭。
senses.why: The word names the male partner of the household bond.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名家庭纽带中的男性一方。

senses.title: To use resources frugally
senses.definition: to manage money, time or supplies carefully so they last
senses.definitionCN: 精打细算地管理钱财、时间或物资使其持久
senses.example: They husbanded their water on the long voyage.
senses.exampleCN: 长途航行中他们省着用水。
senses.why: The old housekeeping sense survives: a husband once managed the house, so husbanding means careful housekeeping of resources.
senses.whyCN: 旧义「持家」得以保留：husband 曾指管家，husbanding 便指像管家那样爱惜资源。

senses.title: To manage land or livestock
senses.definition: to cultivate or manage crops, animals or land
senses.definitionCN: 经营庄稼、牲畜或土地
senses.example: The valley has been husbanded for generations.
senses.exampleCN: 这条山谷被世代经营耕种。
senses.why: Managing a household scales up to managing a farm: same careful keeping.
senses.whyCN: 管家的谨慎放大到经营农场：同样的精心守护。

senses.title: A ship's husband or householder title
senses.definition: a person who manages affairs or property for another, in old use
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法中替他人管理事务或财产的人
senses.example: The ship's husband fitted out the vessel.
senses.exampleCN: 船舶经纪人负责装备这条船。
senses.why: The manager sense detached from marriage and named agents who cared for property.
senses.whyCN: 管理义脱离婚姻，指照管财产的代理人。

intro.en: Husband comes from Old Norse husbondi, house-dweller, the free owner or tenant who keeps a house. The marriage sense narrowed from the manager of a household, and the frugal verb keeps that older meaning alive.
intro.cn: husband 来自古诺斯语 husbondi「住户」，即持屋的自由业主或佃农。婚姻义由「家宅管理者」收窄而来，节俭动词则让旧义存活至今。

items.en: Old Norse husbondi joined hus, house, and bondi, dweller or farmer, one who stays and keeps the land.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 husbondi 由 hus「屋」加 bondi「居住者、农夫」构成，指留居守土之人。

items.en: Old English borrowed husbonda early for a male householder or manager of an estate.
items.cn: 古英语很早就借入 husbonda，指男性户主或庄园管事。

items.en: Middle English husband narrowed to a married man while keeping the sense of one who manages the household.
items.cn: 中古英语 husband 收窄为已婚男子，同时保留「持家者」之义。

items.en: The verb husband appeared in the fifteenth century meaning to manage thriftily, from the housekeeping image.
items.cn: 动词 husband 于十五世纪出现，意为节俭管理，源自持家意象。

items.en: Modern English added husbandry, the farming and thrift noun, and kept the rare agent senses.
items.cn: 现代英语派生 husbandry「农艺、节俭」，并保留罕见的代理人之义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the household family. The meaning group compares marriage words and the frugal verb's near neighbours.
note.cn: 形近组收录「户宅」词族；词义组比较婚姻用词与节俭动词的近邻。

entries.definition: the care and management of crops, animals or resources.
entries.definitionCN: 农艺；节约管理。本词加后缀的名词。

entries.definition: a married woman keeping the house; built from the same hus + bond idea.
entries.definitionCN: 家庭主妇。由同一 hus + bond 构词法造成。

entries.definition: an obsolete spelling still seen in old books; same word, different clothes.
entries.definitionCN: husband 的旧拼写，旧书中仍可见；同词异形。

entries.definition: a husband or wife, either partner.
entries.definitionCN: 配偶。不分性别的正式说法。

entries.definition: a person sharing a life or enterprise, married or not.
entries.definitionCN: 伴侣；合伙人。不限于婚姻。

entries.definition: to protect and save resources, close to the frugal verb sense.
entries.definitionCN: 节约保护资源。接近第 2 义项。

normalIntro.en: These hooks split the word into hus + band, link it to husbandry, and flag the surprise verb.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩把词拆成 hus 加 band，串起 husbandry，并标记那个出人意料的动词。

normal.en: See house + band inside husband: the one bound to the house.
normal.cn: 在 husband 里看到 house 加 band：与屋子绑在一起的人。

normal.en: husbandry hides inside husband; it means careful farming and thrift.
normal.cn: husbandry 藏在 husband 里；意为精细的农事与节俭。

normal.en: As a verb it surprises: husband your savings means spend them slowly.
normal.cn: 作动词很意外：husband your savings 指慢慢花钱。

normal.en: husband and wife is a fixed pair phrase; learn them together.
normal.cn: husband and wife 是固定配对短语，一起记。

normal.en: ex-husband adds the prefix; the house bond is untied.
normal.cn: ex-husband 加了前缀：与屋子的纽带解开了。

abstract.en: One image: a door with a man standing in it, keeping the home.
abstract.cn: 只记一个画面：一扇门前站着守家的男人。

abstract.en: Old law called anyone who kept a house a husband; marriage borrowed the title.
abstract.cn: 旧法把持屋者都叫 husband；婚姻借用了这个头衔。

abstract.en: Frugality is housekeeping in miniature: guard the stores as you guard the door.
abstract.cn: 节俭是缩小的持家：像守门那样看守库存。

examples.en: My husband is the quiet one in our family.
examples.cn: 我丈夫是我们家安静的那位。

examples.en: The city husbanded its fuel during the cold spell.
examples.cn: 寒潮期间该市节约使用燃料。

examples.en: Good husbandry keeps the soil rich year after year.
examples.cn: 精耕细作让土壤年年保持肥沃。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「哈兹笨的」：哈，自家老公有点笨笨的，但是持家可靠。

root: 古诺斯语 husbondi「住户」（hus 屋 + bondi 居住者、农夫），古英语借为 husbonda「户主」；中古英语收窄为「丈夫」，动词义「节俭管理」保留旧义的持家核心。

sensesIntro.en: Husband names the man of the house, keeps the older meaning of managing a household in the frugal verb, extends it to farms and lingers in old agent titles.
sensesIntro.cn: husband 命名一家之男，把更古老的持家义保存在节俭动词里，延伸到农场，并残留在旧职名中。

core.en: The person bound to the house: keeper first, spouse second.
core.cn: 与屋子绑在一起的人：先是守家者，后是配偶。

branches.en: SPOUSE: the modern everyday meaning.
branches.cn: 配偶：现代的日常义。

branches.en: THRIFT: husbanding money, time and supplies.
branches.cn: 节俭：爱惜钱财、时间与物资。

branches.en: LAND: husbanding fields and livestock.
branches.cn: 土地：经营田地与牲畜。

branches.en: AGENT: the old manager and ship's husband.
branches.cn: 代理人：旧时的管事与船舶经纪人。

branches.en: FAMILY: husbandry as the household art that fed the name.
branches.cn: 家业：husbandry 这门持家之术正是名字的来源。

intro.en: Husband builds a small family with husbandry, husbandly and housewife, all from the same house-keeping root.
intro.cn: husband 构成一个小词族：husbandry、husbandly、housewife，全部出自同一「持屋」词根。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries section stays empty; the family is Norse and Germanic, not Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同源词一栏留空；该词族出自诺斯语与日耳曼语，与拉丁语无关。

items.meaning: a married man; to use frugally
items.example: They husbanded every scrap of rope.
Animal husbandry was taught at the college.
Both husbands joined the school trip.
items.exampleCN: 两位丈夫都参加了学校郊游。

items.example: The colony husbanded its seed corn.
Husbanding reserves kept the firm alive.
items.exampleCN: 惜用储备让公司活了下来。

items.example: His husbandly habits kept the shop orderly.
items.exampleCN: 他持家的习惯让店铺井井有条。

items.example: The housewife ran the farm accounts.

items.meaning: an agent who outfits a ship
items.example: The ship's husband bought the new sails.
items.exampleCN: 船舶经纪人购置了新帆。

definition_zh: 容易地；轻松地；很可能；无疑地
definition_en: without difficulty or effort, or very likely and without doubt
core_image: 一片羽毛轻轻松手便滑落
scene: 外婆坐在门口，把毛线针在指间绕得不费力气。 My grandmother easily finishes one sock every evening.
sceneCN: 这里 easily 是「轻松地」（第 1 个义项：不费力地完成某事）；句意：外婆每晚都能轻松织完一只袜子。

forms.label: 副词，由 easy 加 ly 构成

derivatives.zh: easily 的基础形容词，义为「容易的」
同源名词，义为「容易；轻松」

senses.title: Without difficulty
senses.definition: in a way that needs little effort or causes no trouble
senses.definitionCN: 以几乎不需要力气或不引起麻烦的方式
senses.example: My grandmother easily finishes one sock every evening.
senses.exampleCN: 外婆每晚都能轻松织完一只袜子。
senses.why: The action runs smooth because nothing blocks it.
senses.whyCN: 动作顺畅进行，因为没有任何阻碍。

senses.title: Very likely
senses.definition: used to say that something is quite possible
senses.definitionCN: 表示某事很有可能发生
senses.example: The fire could easily spread in dry weather.
senses.exampleCN: 干燥天气里火很容易蔓延。
senses.why: When nothing blocks a thing, it is free to happen.
senses.whyCN: 当没有任何东西阻挡时，事情就容易成真。

senses.title: Without doubt
senses.definition: used to stress that a claim is certainly true
senses.definitionCN: 强调某种说法毫无疑问
senses.example: She is easily the strongest player in the club.
senses.exampleCN: 她无疑是俱乐部里最强的棋手。
senses.why: No effort needed to judge: the answer lies open.
senses.whyCN: 判断毫不费力：答案一目了然。

intro.en: Easily is easy plus ly, and easy itself comes from a Latin word for room and comfort.
intro.cn: easily 是 easy 加 ly，而 easy 源自一个表示「空间、安逸」的拉丁词。

items.en: Latin aptus meant fitted, suited; its Old French descendant aisie meant at ease.
items.cn: 拉丁语 aptus 意为合适的；其古法语后裔 aisie 意为安适的。

items.en: Old French aisie, from aise, ease, described a person without trouble.
items.cn: 古法语 aisie（源自 aise，安逸）形容没有烦恼的人。

items.en: The noun aise meant comfort and room to live.
items.cn: 名词 aise 意为舒适与生活的余地。

items.en: Middle English ese, easy came in as comfort and freedom from pain.
items.cn: 中古英语的 ese、easy 带着舒适与免于痛苦之义进入英语。

items.en: Modern English built easily as the natural adverb of easy.
items.cn: 现代英语把 easily 定为 easy 的自然副词形式。

note.en: These words stand near easily in form or in meaning.
note.cn: 这些词在形式或意义上与 easily 相邻。

entries.definition: becoming less tense or difficult
entries.definitionCN: 缓和；放松

entries.definition: a stand for paintings, different root
entries.definitionCN: 画架（拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: with worry, not at ease
entries.definitionCN: 不安地

entries.definition: with no effort at all
entries.definitionCN: 毫不费力地

entries.definition: without problems or blocks
entries.definitionCN: 顺利地

entries.definition: willingly and without delay
entries.definitionCN: 轻易地；欣然

normalIntro.en: Use the feather-fall picture and the easy family.
normalIntro.cn: 用「羽毛飘落」的画面和 easy 词族来记。

normal.en: easily is easy plus ly, the plain adverb build.
normal.cn: easily 就是 easy 加 ly 的普通副词构造。

normal.en: win easily means the game was never close.
normal.cn: win easily 表示比赛从未胶着。

normal.en: easily damaged warns that small knocks are enough.
normal.cn: easily damaged 提醒轻微碰撞就够造成损坏。

normal.en: easily the best leaves no doubt at all.
normal.cn: easily the best 不留任何疑问。

normal.en: at ease in the army is the same root of comfort.
normal.cn: 军队口令 at ease 用的正是同一「安逸」词根。

abstract.en: Release a feather and watch it drift without effort.
abstract.cn: 放开一根羽毛，看它毫不费力地飘下。

abstract.en: Feel a door that opens before your hand pushes hard.
abstract.cn: 感受一扇没等你用力就先开的门。

abstract.en: See a dry field where any spark would be free to grow.
abstract.cn: 看一片干燥的原野，任何火星都可能轻易成势。

examples.en: The little boy easily lifted the empty box.
examples.cn: 小男孩轻松地举起了空箱子。

examples.en: Glass items break easily when they are packed badly.
examples.cn: 玻璃制品包装不当时很容易打碎。

examples.en: He is easily the kindest person in our class.
examples.cn: 无疑，他是我们班最善良的人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「衣之里」——把手伸进「衣之里」毫不费力就摸到口袋

root: easy 来自拉丁语 aptus（合适的），经古法语 aise（安逸）进入英语；easily 为 easy 加副词后缀 -ly，本义即「处于安逸之中地」。

sensesIntro.en: Easily moves from effortless action to likely events and to claims beyond doubt.
sensesIntro.cn: easily 从毫不费力的动作，延伸到很可能的事件与毫无疑义的断言。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a feather drifting down with no push
core.cn: 核心意象：一根羽毛无需推力便飘然而下

branches.en: The act that meets no block
branches.cn: 毫无阻碍的动作

branches.en: The event with nothing in its way
branches.cn: 无物可挡的事件

branches.en: The judgment that needs no effort
branches.cn: 不费力的判断

branches.en: Whatever flows without resistance
branches.cn: 一切毫无阻力地流动之物

branches.en: The comfort at ease promises
branches.cn: at ease 所许诺的安逸

intro.en: Easily sits in the ease family of comfort and effortlessness.
intro.cn: easily 处在 ease（安逸）词族中，与舒适、不费力相关。

latinIntro.en: The family goes back to Latin aptus, fitted, through Old French aise.
latinIntro.cn: 该词族可回溯到拉丁语 aptus（合适），经古法语 aise 传入。

items.meaning: lack of ease in the body

latinEntries.meaning: fitted, suited; distant source of the ease family
latinEntries.meaningCN: 合适的；ease 词族的远源

definition_zh: 只；仅仅；唯一；只有；不过
definition_en: and nothing or nobody else; no more than; single and without a second one; but, used to introduce a drawback
core_image: 一排同样的杯子被逐个搬走，只有一个留在原来的位置
scene: 仓库清点那天，货架上成排的水杯被一件件搬走，最后只剩一只留在原来的位置。 Only one cup was left on the shelf after the count.
sceneCN: 这里 only 是「唯一的、仅剩的」（第 2 个义项：同类中只有一个）；句意是清点之后货架上只剩一只杯子。画面是空了大半的货架与孤零零的一只杯子。

derivatives.zh: 由 only 与 child 组成的固定说法，义为「独生子女」
由 only 与 begotten 复合而成的古语，义为「独生的；唯一的」
由 only 的词基 one 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「一体；同一性」

senses.title: No more than; and nothing else
senses.definition: no more than a particular number, amount or thing, and nothing in addition
senses.definitionCN: 不超过某个数目、数量或事物，此外再无别的
senses.example: She packed only a small bag for the whole week.
senses.exampleCN: 整整一周她只收拾了一个小包。
senses.why: The word is one plus -ly, and its job is to cut a set down to a single member, so the sense begins as a limit on quantity.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 one 加 -ly 构成，职责是把一个集合削减到单独一个成员，所以词义从「限量」开始。

senses.title: Single and without another
senses.definition: being the single one of its kind, with no second one to choose from
senses.definitionCN: 同类之中只有一个，没有第二个可供选择
senses.example: Only one cup was left on the shelf after the count.
senses.exampleCN: 清点之后，货架上只剩一只杯子。
senses.why: When the same limit is applied to a whole group, the member left is the sole one, and the adverb turns into an adjective of uniqueness.
senses.whyCN: 把同样的限量用在整个群体上，剩下的那一个就成了唯一者，副词于是变成表「唯一」的形容词。

senses.title: Solely, marking the single person or thing that qualifies
senses.definition: used to say that a particular person or thing is the only one that does something or is allowed to do it
senses.definitionCN: 用来说明某人或某物是唯一做某事或获准做某事的一个
senses.example: Only the manager can open that safe.
senses.exampleCN: 只有经理才能打开那个保险柜。
senses.why: Here the cut falls on the doers rather than on the quantity, so the word points at the single agent allowed to act.
senses.whyCN: 这里的削减落在做事的人而不是数量上，所以这个词指向唯一获准行动的那个主体。

senses.title: But; except that
senses.definition: used before a fact that makes what was just said less strong or less happy
senses.definitionCN: 用在某个使前文减弱或令人不那么愉快的事实之前
senses.example: The flat is cheap, only it is far from the station.
senses.exampleCN: 这套房子便宜，只不过离车站太远。
senses.why: A limit on goodness is still a limit, so the same cutting word comes to mark the one flaw that a praise has to admit.
senses.whyCN: 对「好处」加以限制仍然是限制，于是这个表示削减的词转来标出称赞不得不承认的那一处缺陷。

intro.en: Only is one plus the suffix -ly, and it grew from a numeral into a word that limits, singles out and finally concedes.
intro.cn: only 由「一」加后缀 -ly 构成，从数词长成一个表示限量、挑出唯一者、最后表示让步的词。

items.en: The adjective anlic meant one-like or alone, built from an, one, and -lic, the ancestor of -ly.
items.cn: 形容词 anlic 意为「像一的、单独的」，由 an（一）与 -lic（-ly 的前身）构成。

items.en: The adverb anlice limited a statement to a single item, and its spoken form gradually shrank toward only.
items.cn: 副词 anlice 把陈述限制在单独一项上，它的口语形式逐渐缩减为 only。

items.en: Middle English only served both as adjective and adverb, meaning alone, single and no more than.
items.cn: 中古英语的 only 兼作形容词与副词，意为单独的、唯一的、仅仅。

items.en: Later the word gained a concessive use before clauses of objection, as in it is cheap, only it is far.
items.cn: 后来这个词又在表示异议的小句前获得让步用法，如「便宜，只不过太远」。

items.en: Modern English uses only for quantity, for uniqueness, for a single qualifying person, and for a mild objection.
items.cn: 现代英语用 only 表示数量限制、唯一性、唯一符合条件者，以及温和的反对。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same one-plus-suffix pattern; the near-meaning group gathers words of limitation and singleness.
note.cn: 形近组收同样由「一」加后缀构成的词；近义组收表示限制与单独的词语。

entries.definition: The numeral inside only, still meaning a single thing or person.
entries.definitionCN: only 内部那个数词，至今表示单独的一件或一人。

entries.definition: Built in origin on the same one-plus pattern, meaning without others.
entries.definitionCN: 来源上同样由「一」加后缀构成，意为独自、没有别人。

entries.definition: From alone plus -ly, meaning sad at being without company; the spelling is close but the history differs.
entries.definitionCN: 由 alone 加 -ly 构成，意为孤独的；拼写相近，但构词历史不同。

entries.definition: Another adverb built from one, meaning one time; it sounds close but marks a count rather than a limit.
entries.definitionCN: 同样由「一」构成的副词，意为一次；读音相近，但标的是次数而非限量。

entries.definition: Only and nothing more, used to play down what is described.
entries.definitionCN: 仅仅、只不过，用来淡化所描述的事物。

entries.definition: Exactly, or only; often interchangeable with only in limits.
entries.definitionCN: 恰好、仅仅；在表示限制时常可与 only 互换。

entries.definition: For one reason or by one person alone.
entries.definitionCN: 仅仅因为一个原因，或只由一个人。

entries.definition: Single and the only one existing.
entries.definitionCN: 单独的；唯一存在的。

normalIntro.en: The word leaves a single item in view, and its family keeps narrowing a shelf, a group and a sentence down to one member.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词只把一个物件留在视野里，同族用法一再把货架、群体与句子收窄到一个成员。

normal.en: Only is one plus -ly, so its oldest job is to leave a single item in view.
normal.cn: only 是 one 加 -ly，最古老的任务就是只留一个物件在视野里。

normal.en: Alone and lonely share the same one-plus-suffix origin, which is why all three suggest being by oneself.
normal.cn: alone 与 lonely 共用「一」加后缀的来源，所以三者都带「独自」的意味。

normal.en: Only the manager limits the doers, while only a small bag limits the quantity.
normal.cn: only the manager 限制的是做事的人，only a small bag 限制的是数量。

normal.en: Not only opens a set instead of closing it, which is why it pairs with but also.
normal.cn: not only 不是关上一个集合，而是把它打开，所以要与 but also 配合。

normal.en: The concessive only, as in only it is far, marks the single flaw left in a praise.
normal.cn: 表示让步的 only，如 only it is far，标出称赞里剩下的那一处缺陷。

abstract.en: Picture a shelf of identical cups and all but one carried away: the survivor is the thing only points at.
abstract.cn: 想象一货架同样的杯子只只被搬走，只剩一只：留下来的那只就是 only 所指的东西。

abstract.en: A spotlight narrowed to one face explains the word better than a definition, because everything else simply falls outside the beam.
abstract.cn: 把聚光灯收窄到一张脸上，比任何定义都更能解释这个词，因为其余一切都落在光束之外。

abstract.en: The same narrowing falls on a number, a person or a good quality, which is why one small word serves four jobs.
abstract.cn: 同一种收窄可以落在数量、某个人或某处好处上，所以这一个小词能担四项职责。

examples.en: She packed only a small bag for the whole week.
examples.cn: 整整一周她只收拾了一个小包。

examples.en: Only the manager can open that safe.
examples.cn: 只有经理才能打开那个保险柜。

examples.en: The flat is cheap, only it is far from the station.
examples.cn: 这套房子便宜，只不过离车站太远。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「昂立」——昂首立着的只有一个；only 意为只、唯一的。

root: 古英语 anlic（像一的、单独的）由 an（一）加 -lic（-ly 的前身）构成，副词 anlice 逐渐缩为 only；词义从「单独」发展为「只、仅仅、唯一」，再引申出「不过」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is narrowing a set to one; the senses apply that narrowing to quantity, to uniqueness, to the single qualifying agent, and finally to a single flaw.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「把一个集合收窄到一个」；义项把这层收窄依次用在数量、唯一性、唯一符合条件的主体，最后用在一处缺陷上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of identical cups with every one removed except a single cup.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排同样的杯子，除了一只之外都被搬走。

branches.en: a small bag holding a week of clothes
branches.cn: 一只装下一周衣物的小包

branches.en: a shelf with one cup left on it
branches.cn: 货架上只剩一只杯子

branches.en: a manager's key turning in a safe
branches.cn: 经理的钥匙转动保险柜

branches.en: a cheap flat standing far from the station
branches.cn: 便宜却离车站很远的房子

branches.en: the same narrowing, of an amount or of a group
branches.cn: 同一种收窄，落在数量上或群体上

intro.en: The word is held together by the numeral one, the Old English suffix that became -ly, and the forms those two produced.
intro.cn: 这个词由数词「一」、后来变成 -ly 的古英语后缀，以及二者合成的一系列形式支撑。

senses.title: Outer form

senses.title: To form

senses.title: Condition

definition_zh: 社区；社群；团体；社会；共同感
definition_en: a group of people living in one place or sharing interests, work or feelings
core_image: 一群人围着同一口井打水、聊天
scene: 周六上午，我们小区的志愿者一起清扫花园。 Our community cleaned the garden together last Saturday.
sceneCN: 这里 community 是「社区」（第 1 个义项：同一地方居住的人群）；句意是上周六我们社区一起清扫了花园。

senses.title: People living in one place
senses.definition: all the people who live in one area
senses.definitionCN: 住在同一地区的所有人
senses.example: Our community has a small library.
senses.exampleCN: 我们社区有个小图书馆。
senses.why: People who share streets soon share everything else.
senses.whyCN: 共享街道的人们很快共享其他一切。

senses.title: A group with shared interests or work
senses.definition: people linked by job, belief or hobby
senses.definitionCN: 因职业、信仰或爱好相连的人们
senses.example: The school's science community meets every Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 学校的科学社团每周五聚会。
senses.why: Common interests act like invisible streets.
senses.whyCN: 共同兴趣像无形的街道把人连起来。

senses.title: Feeling of belonging together
senses.definition: the sense of sharing and helping one another
senses.definitionCN: 彼此分享、互相帮助的感觉
senses.example: Helping old neighbours builds a real community.
senses.exampleCN: 帮助老邻居能培养真正的社区感。
senses.why: The group becomes one heart, not just many doors.
senses.whyCN: 这个群体成为一颗心，而不只是许多扇门。

items.cn: communitas 意为团体或公共精神。

normal.en: a sense of community means feeling you belong.

normal.en: the business community talks about work together.

abstract.en: Picture neighbours waving from their doorsteps each morning.
abstract.cn: 想象每天早晨邻居们在门口挥手。

abstract.en: Picture hands of many sizes planting one tree together.
abstract.cn: 想象大小不一的手一起种下一棵树。

abstract.en: Picture a bulletin board covered with friendly notes.

examples.en: Students do community service at the old people's home.

examples.en: A strong community helped the family rebuild their house.
examples.cn: 团结的社区帮这家人重建了房屋。

definition_zh: 逃跑；逃脱；逃离；避开；泄漏；逃生
definition_en: to get away from a place, danger or someone's control
core_image: 冲出牢笼：从限制的包围中破口而出
scene: 动物园围栏的门没关好，一只小鸟扑翅而出。 The bird escaped from its open cage at dusk.
sceneCN: 这里 escape 是「逃脱」（第 1 个义项：离开限制之地）；句意是小鸟在黄昏时逃出了敞开的笼子。

collocations.zh: 逃过某人的注意；被忽视

derivatives.zh: 同根加后缀构成的名词，义为「恶作剧；越轨行为」
由 escape 加 -ist 构成，义为「逃避现实的人」
由 escape 加 -ism 构成，义为「逃避主义；自我逃避」

senses.title: To get away from a place
senses.definition: to leave a place where you are kept, or to get out of danger
senses.definitionCN: 离开被关押的地方，或脱离危险
senses.example: The prisoners escaped through a hidden tunnel.
senses.exampleCN: 囚犯们通过一条隐蔽的地道逃走了。
senses.why: The root idea is slipping out of a restraining cloak, so the image is breaking out of an enclosure.
senses.whyCN: 词根本义是从束缚的斗篷中滑出，画面是冲出围困之处。

senses.title: To avoid something unpleasant
senses.definition: to succeed in avoiding something harmful or unwanted
senses.definitionCN: 成功躲开有害或不想遭遇的事
senses.example: The town escaped the worst of the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 这座小镇躲过了风暴最猛烈的袭击。
senses.why: Dangers chase you like keepers chase a prisoner, so dodging them is another way of not being caught.
senses.whyCN: 危险如看守追捕逃犯，躲开它们即另一种「未被抓住」。

senses.title: To leak or get out of a container
senses.definition: of gas, liquid or information, to get out of where it should be held
senses.definitionCN: 气体、液体或信息从本应被容纳之处跑出来
senses.example: Gas was escaping from the broken pipe.
senses.exampleCN: 煤气正从破裂的管道中逸出。
senses.why: What is confined longs to be out, so the same breaking-out image applies to steam and secrets.
senses.whyCN: 被约束之物渴望外出，同样的破围画面也适用于蒸汽与秘密。

senses.title: An act of getting away
senses.definition: the act or way of getting away, or something that frees the mind from daily life
senses.definitionCN: 逃脱的行为或方式，也指让心灵摆脱日常的事
senses.example: Reading is her escape from a busy day.
senses.exampleCN: 读书是她从忙碌一天中解脱的方式。
senses.why: Once the verb is settled, the noun names the break itself, both physical and mental.
senses.whyCN: 动词定型后，名词指那次突破本身，既指身体也指心灵。

intro.en: Escape comes from Vulgar Latin and Old French words about slipping out of a cloak. The picture of getting out of a covering has stayed with the word for a thousand years.
intro.cn: escape 经通俗拉丁语与古法语，本义为「从斗篷中滑脱」。脱出覆盖物的画面伴随这个词上千年。

items.en: Vulgar Latin excappare meant 'to slip out of one's cape', from ex- (out) and cappa (cloak).
items.cn: 通俗拉丁语 excappare 意为「脱出斗篷」，由 ex-（向外）与 cappa（斗篷）构成。

items.en: Old French eschaper kept the meaning 'to get free, to slip away', the cloak still implied.
items.cn: 古法语 eschaper 沿用「脱身、溜走」之意，斗篷意象仍在。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the thirteenth century as escapen, first about prisoners and captives.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入 escapen，最早用于囚犯与被俘者。

items.en: By the seventeenth century the word covered leaking gas and avoiding danger, extending the breakout image.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，词义扩展到气体泄漏与躲避危险，破围意象延伸。

items.en: The mental sense, an escape from daily life, became common in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 「逃离日常」的心理意义在十九世纪变得常用。

note.en: The first group collects the same cloak-root family; the second collects near meanings about getting away.
note.cn: 第一组收集同一「斗篷」词根的词族；第二组收集与「逃离」相关的近义词。

entries.definition: a wild or reckless act of breaking rules
entries.definitionCN: 恶作剧；越轨行为。同根词，指突破规矩的举动。

entries.definition: the habit of avoiding unpleasant reality through fantasy or fun
entries.definitionCN: 逃避主义。由 escape 加 -ism 构成。

entries.definition: a sleeveless cloak; the very garment in the original image
entries.definitionCN: 斗篷；披肩。正是词源画面中的那件衣服。

entries.definition: to run away quickly, often from serious danger
entries.definitionCN: 逃走；逃离。强调急速离开，多用于重大危险。

entries.definition: to avoid cleverly, often duties or questions
entries.definitionCN: 回避；逃避。强调巧妙躲开责任或提问。

entries.definition: to escape suddenly from prison or confinement
entries.definitionCN: 突然逃脱；爆发。多指集体越狱或冲突爆发。

normalIntro.en: Five concrete hooks built from the real cloak root and daily phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 五条基于「斗篷」词根与日常搭配的具体联想。

normal.en: es- means out and cape means cloak: sliding out of the cloak is escaping.
normal.cn: es-（出）+ cape（斗篷）：从斗篷里滑出去，就是逃脱。

normal.en: Cape still names a real cloak today, so the root picture is touchable.
normal.cn: cape 一词至今仍是斗篷，词源画面可见可触。

normal.en: A narrow escape means you almost did not get away.
normal.cn: narrow escape 死里逃生，差点没逃掉，反义衬托。

normal.en: The fire escape is the route out when fire blocks the stairs.
normal.cn: fire escape 太平梯：火灾时的逃生路线。

normal.en: The sound hints at lifting a cover and running, for spelling only.
normal.cn: 谐音：「一斯盖就跑」——掀开覆盖物就跑，帮助拼读，不是词源。

abstract.en: Picture a bird pushing out of a half-open cage at dusk.
abstract.cn: 画面：黄昏时小鸟扑出半开的鸟笼。

abstract.en: Feel the cold air rush in as you slip out of a heavy cloak.
abstract.cn: 动作：从厚重斗篷滑出时冷风灌入的瞬间。

abstract.en: Imagine steam hissing out of a cracked pipe, small but unstoppable.
abstract.cn: 感觉：蒸汽从裂缝嘶嘶逸出，微小却不可阻挡。

examples.en: Two lions escaped from the zoo last night.
examples.cn: 昨晚两只狮子从动物园逃走了。

examples.en: We had a narrow escape on the icy road.
examples.cn: 我们在结冰的路上死里逃生。

examples.en: Some heat escaped from the broken window.
examples.cn: 一些热量从破窗中散失了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一斯盖」——一掀开盖子就跑，谐音帮助拼读，不是词源。

root: escape 源自通俗拉丁语 excappare（ex- 向外 + cappa 斗篷），经古法语 eschaper 进入英语，本义为「脱出斗篷」，核心是挣脱覆盖与束缚。

sensesIntro.en: Escape runs from breaking out of a place, to dodging danger, to leaking out, to the mental break from daily life.
sensesIntro.cn: escape 从冲出某地，到躲开危险，到气体逸出，再到心灵逃离日常，义项沿「脱出」延伸。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: slipping out of a covering or enclosure.
core.cn: 核心意象：从覆盖物或围困中滑脱而出。

branches.en: BREAKING OUT
branches.cn: 囚犯、动物与人离开被禁之地。

branches.en: AVOIDANCE
branches.cn: 小镇躲过风暴、人们躲开责难。

branches.en: LEAKING
branches.cn: 煤气、水与秘密悄悄溜出。

branches.en: MENTAL RELIEF
branches.cn: 以读书或旅行逃离日常。

branches.en: FREEDOM BRANCH
branches.cn: 不再被束缚的共同状态。

intro.en: Escape carries the Latin ex- out-prefix and the cappa cloak root visibly.
intro.cn: escape 清晰保留拉丁 ex-「向外」前缀与 cappa「斗篷」词根。

latinIntro.en: Vulgar Latin excappare is the shared ancestor; the cloak family is small but real.
latinIntro.cn: 通俗拉丁语 excappare 是共同祖先；斗篷词族不大但真实。

items.example: A cape is still worn today.
An escapade is a playful breakout.
Escapism is the habit of escaping reality.
items.exampleCN: escapism 指逃避现实的习性。

items.example: Capture is the opposite of escape.
items.exampleCN: capture 恰是 escape 的反面。

items.example: Buildings mark the fire escape clearly.

pos.zh: 疼痛的；令人痛苦的；艰难的；令人尴尬的

senses.title: Causing physical hurt
senses.definition: causing a feeling of hurt in the body
senses.definitionCN: 引起身体痛感的
senses.example: The wound was still painful when the dressing was changed.
senses.exampleCN: 换药时伤口还在疼。
senses.why: The suffix -ful means full of, so painful describes something full of pain, a thing that gives pain rather than feels it.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ful 表示「充满」，所以 painful 形容某物充满疼痛，是「给出疼痛」而不是「感到疼痛」。

senses.title: Causing deep sadness
senses.definition: making someone feel great sadness or distress
senses.definitionCN: 使人感到巨大悲伤或难受的
senses.example: It was a painful reminder of how much she had lost.
senses.exampleCN: 那是一个令人痛苦的提醒，让她想起自己失去了多少。
senses.why: If a thing can be full of bodily pain, it can also be full of grief, so the word moves from flesh to feeling without changing shape.
senses.whyCN: 既然一个东西能装满身体的痛，也能装满悲伤，于是这个词从皮肉移到情绪，形式却一点没变。

senses.title: Hard to get through
senses.definition: difficult, tiring or unpleasant to experience or perform
senses.definitionCN: 经历或执行起来困难、累人或难受的
senses.example: The first year of the project was a painful process.
senses.exampleCN: 项目的第一年是个艰难的过程。
senses.why: Anything that takes effort feels like a small injury to comfort, which is why painful stretches to mean laborious rather than literally sore.
senses.whyCN: 凡是费力的事都像对舒适的一次小损伤，所以 painful 会引申为「艰难、费力」，而不是字面意义上的「疼」。

senses.title: Awkward and embarrassing
senses.definition: so awkward that people feel uncomfortable and do not know what to say
senses.definitionCN: 尴尬到让人不自在、不知道该说什么的
senses.example: A painful silence followed his question.
senses.exampleCN: 他问完之后是一阵令人尴尬的沉默。
senses.why: Embarrassment is felt as a sting, and English often borrows the language of physical hurt for social discomfort.
senses.whyCN: 尴尬会被感受成一种刺痛，英语常用身体的痛来形容社交上的不适。

intro.en: Painful is an English construction on pain, and pain itself came from a Latin word for penalty through French.
intro.cn: painful 是在 pain 上构成的英语词，而 pain 本身来自拉丁语中表示惩罚的词，经法语传来。

items.en: Poena meant penalty or the price paid for a wrong, and it did not yet name a bodily sensation.
items.cn: poena 意为处罚，或为过错付出的代价，当时还不指身体的感觉。

items.en: Old French peine carried both punishment and hardship into the sense of suffering.
items.cn: 古法语 peine 把「惩罚」和「艰苦」一起带进了「受苦」的意思。

items.en: Middle English pain settled on the hurt a person feels in body or mind.
items.cn: 中古英语的 pain 定在人在身体或心里感到的痛。

items.en: The suffix -ful, from a word meaning full, was added to nouns to mean full of or causing.
items.cn: 后缀 -ful 来自意为「满」的词，加在名词后表示「充满」或「引起」。

items.en: Modern English uses painful for sore wounds, sad news, hard years and awkward quiet alike.
items.cn: 现代英语用 painful 同时形容发疼的伤口、令人难过的消息、艰难的岁月和尴尬的安静。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms built on pain with other endings; the near-meaning group collects adjectives for soreness and distress.
note.cn: 形近组收 pain 接其他词尾构成的形式；近义组收表示酸痛与难受的形容词。

normalIntro.en: Painful is pain plus a suffix that says full of, so every sense asks what kind of pain a thing is full of.
normalIntro.cn: painful 是 pain 加上表示「充满」的后缀，所以每个义项都在问：这个东西装的是哪一种痛。

normal.en: The suffix -ful means full of, so painful names the source of pain while pain names the feeling.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ful 意为充满，所以 painful 指痛的来源，pain 则指痛的感觉。

normal.en: Painless swaps -ful for -less, and the meaning turns to its opposite.
normal.cn: painless 把 -ful 换成 -less，意思就翻到反面。

normal.en: Painfully adds -ly and describes how something is done.
normal.cn: painfully 再加 -ly，描述一件事是以什么方式做的。

normal.en: A painful process hurts without wounding, which shows how far the suffix can stretch.
normal.cn: 艰难的过程并不造成伤口却让人难受，可见这个后缀能伸多远。

normal.en: The base pain came from Latin poena, a penalty, so the family always carries the idea of a cost.
normal.cn: 基础词 pain 来自拉丁语 poena（惩罚），所以这一族词总带着「代价」的想法。

abstract.en: English lets a suffix decide direction: painful is what gives pain, not what feels it.
abstract.cn: 英语让后缀决定方向：painful 是「给出痛」的东西，而不是「感到痛」的。

abstract.en: Calling a silence painful says that embarrassment is a kind of injury we all recognise.
abstract.cn: 把沉默叫作 painful，等于说尴尬是一种人人都认得的损伤。

abstract.en: A word for penalty became a word for hurt, and then a word for anything hard to endure.
abstract.cn: 一个表示惩罚的词先变成「痛」，再变成「任何难以忍受的事」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a thing full of pain; the senses run from a sore body part to grief, to a hard stretch of time, and to social awkwardness.

core.cn: 核心意象：手指碰到还没长好的伤口，整个人一缩。

branches.en: an old photograph that ends the laughter

branches.en: a first year spent learning by failing

branches.en: a table where nobody dares to speak

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语名词 poena 与形容词 poenalis 位于 pain 之后，因此也就在 painful 之后。

definition_zh: 手指；指头；指状物；用手指触碰
definition_en: one of the long parts of the hand, a finger-shaped part, or to touch with fingers
core_image: 手掌伸出的五根细枝：抓、点、数的工具
scene: 钢琴老师轻敲琴键，示意学生跟着按。 She pressed a key with her little finger.

senses.title: One of the parts of the hand
senses.definition: one of the five long bending parts at the end of the hand
senses.definitionCN: 手末端五根可以弯曲的长条部分
senses.example: She wore a ring on her middle finger.
senses.exampleCN: 她中指上戴着一枚戒指。
senses.why: The core image is the hand's five grasping branches, so the first sense names one branch.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是手掌伸出的五根抓握细枝，第一个义项给其中一根命名。

senses.title: A finger-shaped part
senses.definition: a narrow part shaped like a finger, such as part of a glove or a strip of land
senses.definitionCN: 形状像手指的狭长部分，如手套的指部或狭长地块
senses.example: A finger of land stretched into the lake.
senses.exampleCN: 一块狭长的陆地伸进湖里。
senses.why: Anything long and narrow borrows the hand's shape.
senses.whyCN: 一切细长的东西都借用了手掌的形状。

senses.title: To touch or handle with fingers
senses.definition: to touch or play with something using the fingers, often nervously
senses.definitionCN: 用手指触碰或摆弄某物，常带紧张感
senses.example: He fingered the edge of the letter before opening it.
senses.exampleCN: 拆信前他用手指摩挲着信封边缘。
senses.why: The tool itself becomes the verb: the finger acts.
senses.whyCN: 工具本身变成动词：手指自己行动起来。

senses.title: To point out a criminal
senses.definition: to tell the police who committed a crime
senses.definitionCN: 向警方指明罪犯是谁
senses.example: The witness fingered the driver in the line-up.
senses.exampleCN: 证人在辨认队列中指认了那名司机。
senses.why: Pointing uses the finger, so naming a culprit is fingering.
senses.whyCN: 指认要伸手指，于是指认罪犯也用同一个词。

intro.cn: finger 是表示手部细枝的本族日耳曼词。

items.cn: 现代词的基础是日耳曼语中表示手指的词族。

items.cn: 古英语 finger 指手指或脚趾。

items.en: The verb and the criminal-slang sense developed later.

items.en: Modern English keeps the word in daily hand talk.

normalIntro.en: Five hooks, one for each finger.

normal.en: Crossing your fingers is a wish for luck.

normal.en: A finger of land looks like a hand reaching into water.
normal.cn: 指状陆地像伸进水里的手。

normal.en: Finger food is eaten without a fork.
normal.cn: 手抓食物不用叉子。

normal.en: Pointing a finger at someone means blaming them.
normal.cn: 把手指指向某人就是指责。

abstract.en: Fingers are the hand's five explorers.
abstract.cn: 手指是手掌派出的五名探险家。

abstract.en: Every keyboard word begins at a fingertip.
abstract.cn: 键盘上的每个词都始于指尖。

abstract.en: The finger is the smallest bridge between mind and world.
abstract.cn: 手指是心灵与世界之间最细的桥。

examples.en: She counted the coins on her fingers.
examples.cn: 她掰着手指数硬币。

examples.en: Don't point your finger at others so quickly.
examples.cn: 别急着把矛头指向别人。

examples.en: He fingered the keys without playing a sound.
examples.cn: 他手指搭在琴键上却没有出声。

core_image: 一只手把一台小方盒举到眼前
scene: 旅行时，他举起相机拍下了整片山谷。 On the trip he raised his camera and photographed the whole valley.

senses.title: The device for photographs
senses.definition: a device with a lens that takes still photographs
senses.definitionCN: 带镜头、用于拍摄静止照片的设备
senses.example: On the trip he raised his camera and photographed the whole valley.
senses.exampleCN: 旅行时他举起相机拍下了整片山谷。
senses.why: Camera is short for camera obscura, a dark room that focused light to form an image.
senses.whyCN: camera 是 camera obscura 的缩写，原指一个让光线聚焦成像的暗室。

senses.title: The device for video
senses.definition: a device that records moving pictures and sound
senses.definitionCN: 录制活动画面与声音的设备
senses.example: A camera followed the runner along the track.
senses.exampleCN: 一台摄像机沿着跑道跟拍那位跑者。
senses.why: Film and television kept the same Latin name for the machine that records moving images.
senses.whyCN: 电影与电视沿用了同一个拉丁名称，来指录制活动影像的机器。

senses.title: A private legal hearing
senses.definition: a court session held in private and closed to the public
senses.definitionCN: 不向公众开放、私下进行的法庭审理
senses.example: The judge heard the case in camera.
senses.exampleCN: 法官非公开审理了这起案件。
senses.why: In camera literally means in a chamber, and English law borrowed it for hearings held in a closed room.
senses.whyCN: in camera 字面意思是「在房间里」，英国法律借它指在关闭的房间内进行的审理。

intro.en: Camera is short for camera obscura, Latin for a dark room, because early cameras were darkened boxes that focused light.
intro.cn: camera 是 camera obscura 的缩写，拉丁语意为「暗室」，因为早期相机就是让光线聚焦的暗箱。

items.en: Camera meant a room or chamber in Latin.
items.cn: camera 在拉丁语中意为房间或室。

items.en: A camera obscura was a dark room with a small hole that threw an image on the wall.
items.cn: camera obscura 是一间开小孔的暗室，能把影像投在墙上。

items.en: Portable dark boxes replaced the room and kept the name camera.
items.cn: 便携的暗箱取代了房间，却保留了 camera 这个名字。

items.en: When light-sensitive plates appeared, the box became a camera that fixed the image.
items.cn: 当感光板出现，这个暗箱就成了能固定影像的照相机。

items.en: Today camera covers still, video and phone cameras, and the legal phrase in camera survives.
items.cn: 今天 camera 涵盖照相机、摄像机和手机镜头，法律短语 in camera 也仍在使用。

abstract.en: Picture the raised box whenever you hear the click of a shutter.
abstract.cn: 每次听到快门的咔嚓声，就想起那个举到眼前的盒子。

root: camera 是 camera obscura 的缩写，拉丁语意思是「暗室」。最早人们在一间关黑、只开小孔的房间外观察，光线穿过小孔会在墙上投出倒立的影像。后来这种房间被做成便携的暗箱，名字仍是 camera。感光板出现后，暗箱能够把影像固定下来，于是成了照相机；录制活动画面的机器沿用同一名称，成了摄像机。法律里 in camera 仍保留「在房间内」的旧义，指不公开的审理。

sensesIntro.en: The three senses of camera grow from one picture: a dark box that catches light and keeps an image.
sensesIntro.cn: camera 的三个义项都从同一个画面生长出来：一个接住光线、留住影像的暗箱。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small dark box raised to one eye
core.cn: 核心意象：一只被举到眼前的小暗箱

branches.en: THE STILL CAMERA: the box that fixes one picture is the first sense.
branches.cn: 静照线：固定单幅画面的盒子是第一个义项。

branches.en: THE VIDEO CAMERA: the same box records motion.
branches.cn: 录像线：同一个盒子用来记录运动。

branches.en: THE CLOSED ROOM: the old legal phrase keeps the room sense.
branches.cn: 密室线：古老的法律短语保留了房间义。

branches.en: THE LENS: both still and moving pictures pass through the same glass.
branches.cn: 镜头线：静照与录像都经过同一片玻璃。

branches.en: THE PRIVATE VIEW: what the camera sees may stay closed to the public.
branches.cn: 私下线：镜头看到的内容也可以不向公众公开。

intro.en: Camera is a base noun, so the items below are its endings and the words it joins.
intro.cn: camera 是基础名词，下面列出的是它的词尾以及与之组合的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin camera, a room, and obscura, dark, are the recorded words behind the name camera obscura.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 camera（房间）与 obscura（暗的）是 camera obscura 这个名字背后的有记录词形。

items.meaning: a person who works with it

definition_zh: 意思是；意味着；打算；平均值；中间值；刻薄的；吝啬的
definition_en: to intend or signify something; also the middle value of a set of numbers, or unkind and unwilling to spend
core_image: 一句含混的话被手指向它真正要说的那件事，旁边天平恰好停在正中
scene: 统计员把五个读数的总和除开，求出中间的那个数值。 The mean of the five readings is nine.
sceneCN: 这里指「一组数的平均值」（第 4 个义项：平均数）；句意为五个读数的平均值是九。可辨识物件：记录纸、五个读数、计算器、天平；对应第 1 个义项。

有意义的

senses.title: To have a sense
senses.definition: to have as a meaning, said of a word, sign or gesture
senses.definitionCN: 指词语、符号或手势所具有的意思
senses.example: What does this symbol mean?
senses.exampleCN: 这个符号表示什么？
senses.why: The Old English verb mænan meant 'to intend, signify', and a word's sense is what it intends.
senses.whyCN: 古英语动词 mænan 意为「意图、意指」，而词的意思就是它所意图的东西。

senses.title: To be a sign of
senses.definition: to be a sign or indication of something else
senses.definitionCN: 作为另一件事的迹象或征兆
senses.example: A red sky at night means fair weather tomorrow.
senses.exampleCN: 傍晚的红霞意味着明天天气晴好。
senses.why: A sign points to what it intends, so the verb extends from words to natural signs.
senses.whyCN: 符号指向它所意指之物，于是这个动词从词语扩展到自然征兆。

senses.title: To intend to do
senses.definition: to have something in mind as a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 把某事放在心里作为目的
senses.example: I mean to finish the report tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 我打算今晚把报告写完。
senses.why: Intention is the inward side of meaning: what a person means is what he intends.
senses.whyCN: 意图是「意思」的内面：一个人意指什么，就是他打算什么。

senses.title: The average of a set
senses.definition: the value obtained by adding all the numbers and dividing by how many there are
senses.definitionCN: 把全部数值相加再除以个数所得的值
senses.example: Add the values and divide by five to get the mean.
senses.exampleCN: 把这些值相加再除以五，就得到平均值。
senses.why: This sense comes from a different source: Old French meien 'middle', from Latin medianus, not from the English verb.
senses.whyCN: 这一义出自另一来源：古法语 meien「中间」，上溯拉丁 medianus，与英语动词无关。

senses.title: The middle between extremes
senses.definition: a middle point equally distant from two extremes
senses.definitionCN: 与两个极端等距的中间点
senses.example: The golden mean lies between excess and defect.
senses.exampleCN: 中庸之道位于过度与不足之间。
senses.why: The same 'middle' sense serves ethics as well as arithmetic, naming the point that is neither too much nor too little.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「中间」义既用于算术也用于伦理，指既不过多也不过少的那一点。

senses.title: Unkind in manner
senses.definition: unkind, spiteful or deliberately hurtful
senses.definitionCN: 不友善、带恶意或故意伤人的
senses.example: It was mean of him to laugh at her mistake.
senses.exampleCN: 他嘲笑她的错误，未免刻薄。
senses.why: The adjective comes from a third source, Old English gemæne 'common, shared', whose sense sank from 'common' to 'inferior' and then to 'petty'.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词出自第三个来源，古英语 gemæne「共同的、共享的」，词义从「共同」降到「低劣」，再降到「小气」。

senses.title: Stingy with money
senses.definition: unwilling to spend or share what one has
senses.definitionCN: 不愿花钱或不愿分享所有
senses.example: He is too mean to buy a second chair.
senses.exampleCN: 他太吝啬，连第二把椅子都不肯买。
senses.why: A person who keeps everything for himself is 'common' in the old sense of ordinary and small, and the word settled into stinginess.
senses.whyCN: 把一切都留给自己的人在旧义上显得「普通而小气」，于是这个词固定为吝啬。

senses.title: Remarkable in the phrase 'no mean'
senses.titleCN: 固定说法中意为「不小的」
senses.definition: not small or easy, used in the fixed phrase no mean feat
senses.definitionCN: 不小、不容易，用于固定说法「不小的成就」
senses.example: Finishing the climb in one day was no mean feat.
senses.exampleCN: 一天之内爬完这段路可不是小事。
senses.why: The phrase works by understatement: it denies the small reading of the adjective in order to praise.
senses.whyCN: 这个说法用反语：否定形容词「小」的那一面，从而达到称赞。

intro.en: Mean has three separate sources that happen to share one spelling: the verb 'to intend' from Old English mænan, the noun 'average' from Old French meien and Latin medianus, and the adjective 'petty, stingy' from Old English gemæne 'common'.
intro.cn: mean 有三个恰好同形的来源：表示「意图」的动词出自古英语 mænan；表示「平均值」的名词出自古法语 meien 与拉丁 medianus；表示「小气、刻薄」的形容词出自古英语 gemæne「共同的」。

items.en: Mænan meant 'to intend, signify'. Its deeper Germanic origin is not settled; the usual comparison with German meinen is a family resemblance rather than a proved derivation.
items.cn: mænan 意为「意图、意指」。其更早的日耳曼来源无定论；通常把它与德语 meinen 相比，那只是同族相似，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Gemæne meant 'common, shared'. The sense passed from 'common' to 'ordinary, inferior' and then to 'petty, stingy', a downward slide recorded in Middle English.
items.cn: gemæne 意为「共同的、共享的」。词义从「共同」经「普通、低劣」滑向「小气、吝啬」，这一下移在中古英语中已有记录。

items.en: Meien 'middle' entered English in the fourteenth century as the name of the middle value, and it is the source of the average sense.
items.cn: meien「中间」在十四世纪进入英语，指居中的那个数值，是平均值义的来源。

items.en: Medianus 'of the middle' comes from medius 'middle', the same root that gives median, medium and mediate.
items.cn: medianus「中间的」出自 medius「中间」，同一词根还给出 median、medium、mediate。

items.en: English spelling merged the three histories into one written form, which is why a single entry must keep verb, average and adjective apart.
items.cn: 英语拼写把这三段历史并成一个书写形式，因此同一个词条必须把动词、平均值与形容词分开。

items.en: Exact first citations for each strand are approximate: the verb is Old English, the average noun is fourteenth-century, and the stingy adjective is later Middle English.
items.cn: 三条线索的确切首见书证都只是约数：动词属古英语，平均值名词属十四世纪，吝啬形容词属中古英语后期。

note.en: Group one holds forms and relatives that are easily mistaken for the same word; group two holds words that share one of the three meanings.
note.cn: 第一组是容易被当成同一个词的形式与亲属词；第二组是分别与三种含义之一相近的词。

entries.definition: The third-person singular of the verb, and separately a plural noun meaning 'resources'; it is not the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 动词的第三人称单数，另有一个表示「资源、手段」的复数名词；都不是那个形容词。

entries.definition: The past tense and participle of the verb; the spelling no longer shows the vowel of the base.
entries.definitionCN: 动词的过去式与过去分词；拼写已看不出原形元音。

entries.definition: From the same Latin root as the average sense, but it names the middle item of an ordered set, not the sum divided by the count.
entries.definitionCN: 与平均值义同出拉丁词根，但指按序排列后居中的那一项，而非总和除以个数。

entries.definition: Latin medius as a noun: the middle, or a means between two sides; it has nothing to do with intending.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁 medius 的名词形式：中间，或两端之间的媒介；与「意图」无关。

entries.definition: The everyday word for the sum divided by the count; mean is its technical doublet in statistics.
entries.definitionCN: 日常说法，指总和除以个数；在统计中 mean 是它的技术性同义词。

entries.definition: To be a sign of something, close to the 'be a sign' sense of mean.
entries.definitionCN: 作为某事的符号，接近 mean 的「预示」义。

entries.definition: To have a purpose, the plain equivalent of the 'plan' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 怀有目的，是「打算」义的直白对应词。

entries.definition: Unwilling to spend or share, the direct synonym of the adjective in its money sense.
entries.definitionCN: 不愿花钱或分享，是形容词在钱财义上的直接同义词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定说法与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Three histories share one spelling: intend, middle, and common-turned-petty.
normal.cn: 三段历史共用一种拼写：意图、中间、由「共同」转来的小气。

normal.en: The verb is irregular in sound but regular in pattern: means, meant, meant, meaning.
normal.cn: 动词读音不规则但形式规律：三单、过去式、过去分词、现在分词依次为 means、meant、meant、meaning。

normal.en: Fixed phrases sort the senses: mean to do, mean well, the mean value, no mean feat.
normal.cn: 固定说法把义项分开：打算做、出于好意、平均值、不小的成就。

normal.en: The average sense came through French, so it belongs with median and medium rather than with the verb.
normal.cn: 平均值义经法语而来，因此它与 median、medium 同族，而不属于动词那一支。

normal.en: The unkind sense began as 'common', which then meant 'ordinary' and finally 'petty'.
normal.cn: 刻薄义起于「共同的」，再变成「普通的」，最后成了「小气的」。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pointing at the one thing a vague sentence was trying to say.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手指出一句含混的话真正想说的那件事。

abstract.en: Picture a pair of scales settling exactly level, with equal weights on both sides.
abstract.cn: 想象一架天平恰好停在水平位置，两边重量相等。

abstract.en: Picture a man counting coins twice before he will spend a single one.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人把硬币数了两遍才肯花掉一枚。

examples.en: A green light means that the road is clear.
examples.cn: 绿灯表示道路畅通。

examples.en: The mean of the class scores rose after the extra lesson.
examples.cn: 加课之后，全班成绩的平均值上升了。

examples.en: It was mean of them to leave her out of the invitation.
examples.cn: 他们把她排除在邀请之外，实在刻薄。

dict_mnemonic.text: 动词那一支表示「意图、意指」；平均值那一支来自法语里的「中间」；形容词那一支从「共同的」滑到「普通」，再滑到「小气」。三支同形，要按上下文分开。

root: 三条互不同源的线索合成一个拼写：动词出自古英语 mænan「意图、意指」，更早来源无定论；平均值义出自古法语 meien「中间」，上溯拉丁 medianus、medius；形容词义出自古英语 gemæne「共同的」，词义下滑为「低劣、小气」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses come from three histories: intending and signifying, the middle value, and the small or petty. The entry keeps them apart so that no sentence is read through the wrong history.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项来自三段历史：意图与意指、居中的数值、以及小气刻薄。本词条把它们分开，免得用错历史去读一个句子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand points at what a sentence intends, while a balance beside it rests exactly level.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手指出一句话所意图的东西，旁边的天平恰好水平。

branches.en: SIGNIFY: a word and a red sky both point to what they intend.
branches.cn: 意指：一个词与一片红霞都指向它们所意图的东西。

branches.en: INTEND: purpose is what a person means to do.
branches.cn: 意图：目的就是一个人打算做的事。

branches.en: THE MIDDLE: the average and the golden mean are one position seen numerically and ethically.
branches.cn: 中间：平均值与中庸是同一点在数字与伦理上的两个看法。

branches.en: COMMON TO PETTY: the adjective slid from shared to ordinary to stingy.
branches.cn: 由共同到小气：形容词从「共享」滑到「普通」再到「吝啬」。

branches.en: UNDERSTATEMENT: denying 'small' is a way of saying 'large'.
branches.cn: 反语：否定「小」，正是说「大」。

intro.en: One spelling serves three families, so the affix view must be split: a Germanic verb, a Germanic adjective, and a Latin root for the middle.
intro.cn: 一种拼写服务于三个词族，因此按语素读时必须拆开：一个日耳曼动词、一个日耳曼形容词，以及一个表示「中间」的拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: The verb family is Germanic, with no Latin kin; the average sense belongs to Latin medius, which also gives median, medium and mediate.
latinIntro.cn: 动词一族属日耳曼语，没有拉丁同族；平均值义属拉丁 medius，同根还给出 median、medium、mediate。

items.example: The Old English verb is the source of the 'signify' senses.
items.exampleCN: 这个古英语动词是「意指」诸义的来源。

items.example: The adjective began as 'shared' and ended as 'stingy'.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词从「共享」开始，最后落到「吝啬」。

items.example: The Latin root supplies the average and middle senses.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁词根提供平均值与中间诸义。
这个派生形容词给出 median。

items.meaning: in a petty or stingy way
items.example: He spoke meanly of the offer.
items.exampleCN: 他刻薄地评价那个提议。

items.meaning: the quality of being petty or stingy
items.exampleCN: 他们的吝啬让客人吃惊。
